## Before the architecture: App Store vs. home-screen web app

**The honest conflict.** Lovable builds React web apps — websites. It cannot produce a file you submit to the App Store or Google Play. Those are two fundamentally different things, and this is your first real decision.

---

**Option A — Progressive Web App (PWA) via Lovable**
A PWA is a website that *behaves* like an app: it has its own icon, loads full-screen, and works on any phone. It fits inside Lovable and your $50 budget.

*What your customers give up:*
- They cannot find it by searching the App Store or Google Play — they need a link from you (text, flyer, QR code)
- On iPhone, installation requires an extra step: open in Safari → tap Share → "Add to Home Screen" — most people don't know to do this
- Notifications are more limited (iOS only supports web push since iOS 16.4, and only after the user has added the app to their home screen)
- It feels slightly less "real" to less tech-savvy customers

---

**Option B — App-store native app via Expo**
Expo is a tool (different from Lovable) that writes one codebase and produces a real iPhone + Android app, published to both stores. It can be used without a terminal through its cloud build service (EAS Build).

*What you give up:*
- Different build tool — not Lovable
- Apple Developer Program: ~$99/year (check current fee at developer.apple.com/programs)
- Google Play Console: ~$25 one-time (check current fee at play.google.com/console)
- Every update goes through Apple review (typically 1–3 days), so you can't ship a fix instantly
- Store payment rules must be checked — Apple and Google change them
- Exceeds your $50/month budget once you add cloud build costs

---

**My recommendation: Option A (PWA).** Lovable can only make web apps, so Option B requires scrapping your chosen build tool. For a solo-operator business where Marisol hands customers the link directly, a PWA is genuinely sufficient for V1. You can revisit a native app if the business grows and customers demand App Store presence. I'll note clearly what your customers asked for and where the gap is.

> **Note to Marisol:** Your customers asked for "a real app I can find in the App Store." With a PWA, they can't. Every new customer needs to receive your link first (text, business card, Instagram bio, QR code on your van). If this is a dealbreaker — if you specifically need App Store discoverability — you'll need to switch build tools and revisit this stage. Just say so.

# ARCHITECTURE.md

## 1. Stack Decision

> **Plain-English glossary for this section:**
> - **Backend/API** — the hidden half of the app that lives on a server, handles rules, and talks to other services; the browser can't see its secrets
> - **Database** — a structured place to store and query all your data (bookings, customers, dogs)
> - **Auth** — the system that handles sign-up, login, and "who is this person?"
> - **Serverless function** — a small piece of server code that runs on demand without you managing a server
> - **Row Level Security (RLS)** — a database feature where each row has rules about who is allowed to read or change it; enforced at the database itself, not just in the UI

| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected alternative & why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | **React** (Lovable generates this) | Lovable decides; no choice | — |
| Backend / API | **Supabase Edge Functions** (serverless functions) | Native Lovable integration; runs server-side so secrets stay off the browser; no terminal needed to write/deploy | Firebase Cloud Functions — less native Lovable support, separate console, more configuration |
| Database | **Supabase PostgreSQL** | Comes bundled with Supabase; has Row Level Security to enforce privacy rules at the data layer | PlanetScale / MongoDB — no built-in auth or storage, extra service to manage |
| Auth | **Supabase Auth** | Bundled with Supabase; handles login, sign-up, JWT tokens (explained in §4), and role claims | Auth0 — starts at ~$23+/month, over budget |
| File storage | **Supabase Storage** | Bundled; supports private buckets and expiring signed URLs (links that expire after an hour) for dog photos | Cloudinary — extra account, extra service, free tier limits on transforms |
| Payments | **Stripe** | You already have an account; industry standard; no monthly fee | PayPal — worse developer API, confusing UX for deposits |
| SMS / notifications | **Twilio** | Best-in-class SMS API; programmatic day-before reminders; straightforward Edge Function integration | AWS SNS — requires AWS console comfort; Postmark/Resend — email only, not SMS |
| Hosting | **Lovable** (frontend) + **Supabase** (backend) | Lovable hosts the web app; Supabase hosts everything else; zero extra services | Vercel — would require moving outside Lovable's managed environment |

*No AI/LLM layer needed for V1.*

---

## 2. System Diagram

> **Plain-English note:** The yellow box is "untrusted" — meaning anyone can open browser dev tools and read everything inside it. The green box is "trusted" — it runs on Supabase's servers and customers can't inspect it. Secret keys live only in the green box.

```mermaid

        FE["React App\nserved by Lovable"]
    end

    subgraph Supabase["🟢 Supabase Cloud (Trusted — server-side)"]
        AUTH["Auth Service\nIssues signed login tokens\nStores role: customer | groomer"]
        DB["PostgreSQL Database\nRow Level Security active\nBookings · Dogs · Profiles"]
        STORAGE["File Storage\nPrivate bucket\nDog photos only"]
        EF["Edge Functions\nHolds all secret keys\nStripe logic · SMS logic"]

    FE -->|"Login / sign-up"| AUTH

    EF -->|"STRIPE_SECRET_KEY 🔐\ncreate payment intent\nverify webhook"| STRIPE

    DB -.->|"RLS policy: customers\nsee own rows only"| DB

    style Browser fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#ffc107

```

---

## 3. Data Model

> **Plain-English note:** A **foreign key** is like a reference — a booking "points at" a customer row so you know whose booking it is. An **index** is a shortcut that makes the database find rows faster without scanning the whole table.

### Table: `profiles`
*(One row per user — both customers and Marisol. Extends Supabase's built-in `auth.users`.)*

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key; same value as `auth.users.id` |
| `name` | `text` | Full name |
| `phone` | `text` | For SMS reminders — **private** |
| `address` | `text` | Home address — **private** |
| `role` | `text` | `'customer'` or `'groomer'` — set once at account creation; **NOT editable by the user** |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | Auto-set |

*Indexes:* `role` (Marisol's day-view queries filter by this)

---

### Table: `dogs`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key |
| `customer_id` | `uuid` | Foreign key → `profiles.id` |
| `name` | `text` | |
| `breed` | `text` | |
| `notes` | `text` | e.g. "gets anxious, needs extra time" |
| `photo_url` | `text` | Storage path in Supabase — fetched via expiring signed URL |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | Auto-set |

*Indexes:* `customer_id`

---

### Table: `bookings`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key |
| `customer_id` | `uuid` | Foreign key → `profiles.id` |
| `dog_id` | `uuid` | Foreign key → `dogs.id` |
| `slot_time` | `timestamptz` | Date + time of the appointment |
| `status` | `text` | `'pending'` / `'confirmed'` / `'cancelled'` / `'completed'` |
| `deposit_paid` | `boolean` | Default `false`; set to `true` by Edge Function after Stripe confirms |
| `stripe_payment_intent_id` | `text` | Stripe's reference ID for the $20 deposit transaction |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | Auto-set |

*Indexes:* `customer_id`, `slot_time`, `(slot_time, status)` composite (prevents double-booking)

*Constraint:* Unique on `slot_time` where `status != 'cancelled'` — two bookings cannot exist for the same slot.

---

### ACCESS RULES

> These map directly to Supabase Row Level Security policies — enforced at the database, not the UI.

| Entity | Who can **read** | Who can **create** | Who can **update** | Who can **delete** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | Own row only (customer) · ALL rows (groomer) | Auth system at sign-up only | Own row — **`role` field is excluded from updates** | Nobody |
| `dogs` | Own dogs only (customer) · ALL dogs (groomer) | Customer — own `customer_id` only | Customer — own dogs only | Customer — own dogs only |
| `bookings` | Own bookings only (customer) · ALL bookings (groomer) | Customer — own `customer_id` only | Customer: `status` → `'cancelled'` only · Groomer: any field | Nobody (cancel by setting status) |

> **Privacy enforcement for the spec's "must NEVER" line:** A customer querying `profiles` gets back exactly one row — their own. The RLS policy reads: `auth.uid() = id`. They cannot reach another customer's `address` or `phone` through any query, because the database rejects it before the data is returned.

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

> **Plain-English note:** A **JWT token** (JSON Web Token) is a signed digital pass issued by the server after login. The browser holds it to prove identity on each request, but can't forge it because it's signed with a secret key only the server knows.

### What runs in the browser (untrusted — assume customers can see everything here)

| Item | Safe to be here? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Supabase `anon` key | ✅ Yes | This is a *public* key — it only permits what RLS allows; Supabase designed it to be exposed |
| JWT login token | ✅ Acceptable | Stored in browser `localStorage` by Supabase SDK; can't be forged; expires |
| React app code | ✅ Yes | UI only |

### What runs on the server (trusted — Edge Functions only)

| Item | Lives here | Never in browser? |
|---|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Edge Function env var | ✅ Never |
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` + `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Edge Function env var | ✅ Never |
| Supabase `service_role` key | Edge Function env var | ✅ Never |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Edge Function env var | ✅ Never |
| Role assignment / permission checks | Edge Functions + RLS | ✅ Never in browser logic |

---

### ⚠️ Lovable-specific warning

Lovable's AI code generator occasionally puts sensitive keys directly in the React frontend — especially the Supabase `service_role` key and, sometimes, Stripe keys. **Before you go live:**

1. Open Lovable's code view and search (Ctrl+F / Cmd+F) for: `service_role`, `sk_live_`, `sk_test_`, `TWILIO_AUTH`
2. If any of these appear outside an Edge Function file, **stop and do not publish** — move them to Supabase Edge Function environment variables instead.

This is the single most important security check for this project.

---

### Where roles are stored and why users can't change them

- Marisol's role (`'groomer'`) and every customer's role (`'customer'`) live in the `profiles.role` column in the database.
- The RLS policy on `profiles` explicitly **excludes `role` from the columns a user can update** — even if someone sends a crafted API request trying to set their own role to `'groomer'`, the database refuses it.
- The role is also embedded in the JWT by Supabase when it issues the token, and the JWT is signed server-side — it cannot be modified by the user.
- The role is **not** stored in browser `localStorage`, cookies, or any client-editable location.

---

### File storage rules

| File type | Bucket | Public? | How it's accessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dog photos | `dogs-photos` | ❌ Private | Supabase generates a signed URL (expires in 1 hour); only the dog's owner or the groomer can request one |
| No other files | — | — | — |

There are no publicly accessible files. A direct URL to a photo returns an error without a valid signed token.

---

## 5. External Services

| Service | Purpose | Key(s) | Where stored | Free tier | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, auth, storage, serverless functions, scheduler | `anon` key (browser-safe), `service_role` key (server only) | `service_role` in Edge Function env vars only | 500 MB database · 1 GB storage · 50,000 monthly active users · 500K Edge Function calls | App stops working entirely; Supabase publishes a status page at status.supabase.com |
| **Stripe** | $20 deposit collection; webhook to confirm payment | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Edge Function env vars only | No monthly fee; 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction (~$0.88 on a $20 deposit) | Customers can't pay deposit; show a clear error and let them retry; no data is lost |
| **Twilio** | SMS reminder the day before each appointment | `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Edge Function env vars only | Free trial covers ~$15 in credits; then ~$0.0079/SMS (US) + ~$1.15/month for a phone number (verify current rates at twilio.com/pricing) | Day-before reminders don't send; Marisol should have a manual backup for busy periods |

---

### In-app purchase note (relevant if you ever go native)

Because GroomGo charges for an **in-person physical service** (dog grooming at a customer's home), Apple and Google generally **do not require their in-app purchase system** — Stripe can be used directly. This is unlike apps selling digital features or subscriptions inside the app. However, store rules change; verify this on Apple's and Google's developer sites before any App Store submission. If you ever add an in-app upgrade or digital feature, Apple and Google typically take 15–30%.

---

## 6. Cost at 0 / 100 / 1,000 Users

> "Monthly active users" = unique people who log in that month. Stripe fees are on transactions, not users.

| Service | 0 users/month | 100 users/month | 1,000 users/month |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lovable (hosting + builder) | Free tier (limited build credits) | Check lovable.dev — Pro plan likely needed for custom domain | Same Pro plan |
| Supabase | $0 (free tier) | $0 (free tier) | ~$25/month Pro (free tier caps near 500 MAU) |
| Stripe fees | $0 | ~$9 (~10 deposits × $0.88 fee) | ~$88 (~100 deposits × $0.88 fee) — comes out of deposit revenue |
| Twilio (number + SMS) | ~$1.15 (just the number) | ~$2 (number + ~100 SMS) | ~$9 (number + ~1,000 SMS) |
| **Estimated total** | **~$1–$26** | **~$12–$36** | **~$122–$147** |

> **Budget note:** At up to ~100 active users per month, you stay comfortably under $50 (assuming Lovable Pro). At 1,000 users, you exceed it — but by then Stripe fees are coming out of deposit revenue, and a $25 Supabase upgrade is easy to justify. Check Lovable's current pricing before building; it's the largest fixed cost.

---

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

1. **ADR-1:** Use Lovable for the frontend because it is the chosen build tool and requires no terminal.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase as the entire backend because Lovable integrates with it natively, and it covers database, auth, storage, and serverless functions in one dashboard with no terminal required.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Row Level Security (RLS) for all privacy rules because it enforces "customers never see other customers' data" at the database level, not just in the UI.
4. **ADR-4:** Store the user role in `profiles.role` in the database (not in browser storage or editable profile fields) because customers must never be able to elevate their own permissions.
5. **ADR-5:** Use Stripe for deposits because the user already has an account and it handles webhooks cleanly with Edge Functions.
6. **ADR-6:** Use Twilio for SMS reminders because automated day-before texts require a real phone SMS API; browser push notifications are too unreliable on iPhone.
7. **ADR-7:** All Stripe and Twilio calls go through Supabase Edge Functions because secret keys must never reach the browser.
8. **ADR-8:** Build as a PWA (progressive web app), not a native app, because Lovable cannot produce App Store builds and the budget doesn't support a second build tool.
9. **ADR-9:** Store dog photos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them via expiring signed URLs because photos are personal data and must never be publicly accessible by direct URL.
10. **ADR-10:** Use Supabase's built-in cron scheduler to trigger the daily reminder Edge Function because it requires no extra service and no terminal work.

---

## 8. Known Risks

**Risk 1: Lovable generates a secret key in the frontend**
*What goes wrong:* Anyone who opens browser dev tools can steal your Stripe or Twilio credentials, charge customers, or send SMS as you.
*Mitigation:* Before going live, search all generated code for `sk_`, `service_role`, and `TWILIO_AUTH`. If found anywhere outside an Edge Function, fix it before publishing — this is non-negotiable.

---

**Risk 2: Stripe webhook not verified**
*What goes wrong:* Stripe sends your server a message saying "payment succeeded" when a deposit is paid. If you don't check the message's signature, anyone on the internet could send a fake message and mark bookings as paid without paying.
*Mitigation:* The Edge Function that handles Stripe webhooks must verify the `Stripe-Signature` header using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Lovable may not generate this automatically — double-check it.

---

**Risk 3: Twilio SMS blocked as spam (A2P 10DLC)**
*What goes wrong:* US mobile carriers now require businesses to register their texting number through a system called A2P 10DLC before sending messages at scale. Unregistered numbers get filtered or blocked.
*Mitigation:* Start A2P 10DLC registration on Twilio the moment you create your account. It typically takes **1–3 weeks** to approve. Do not launch SMS reminders before registration completes.

---

**Risk 4: Double-booking the same time slot**
*What goes wrong:* Two customers click "book 10 AM Thursday" at the same time. Both see it as available. Marisol gets two appointments she can't do.
*Mitigation:* Add a unique database constraint on `slot_time` where `status != 'cancelled'`. The second booking attempt returns an error, and the UI shows "That slot was just taken — pick another."

---

**Risk 5: Supabase free tier limits hit mid-operation**
*What goes wrong:* Supabase pauses free-tier projects that exceed storage or have been idle. Customers can't book; Marisol can't see her route.
*Mitigation:* Watch the Supabase dashboard usage meter. When you approach 80% of any limit (storage, MAU, or bandwidth), upgrade to the $25/month Pro plan. Set a calendar reminder to check it monthly.

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website that lives on phones, not an App Store app.** Lovable can only make websites. Customers get to yours through a link — Marisol texts it to them, puts it on a business card, or adds it as a QR code on her van. Once they open it, they can save it to their home screen so it looks like a regular app. They will not find it by searching "GroomGo" in the App Store.

- **All customer data lives in one locked vault.** Supabase is like a safe that holds every booking, address, dog photo, and phone number. The lock is set so that each customer can only open their own drawer — even if a technically clever person tries to peek at someone else's address, the safe just says no. This isn't a design trick; it's enforced by the database itself.

- **The money flows through your existing Stripe account.** When a customer pays their $20 deposit, the transaction is handled by Stripe and the secret keys that authorize it never leave the server. The customer's phone only sends a "start the payment" message; the server does the actual charging.

- **Reminder texts go out by themselves, the day before.** Every morning, a silent automated job checks which appointments are tomorrow and sends each customer a text via Twilio. Marisol doesn't have to do anything. The catch: you need to register your Twilio phone number with US carriers first, which takes up to three weeks, so start that early.

- **You're under budget at your current scale.** At up to about 100 customers per month, total costs stay below $50. Stripe fees come directly out of deposit revenue, so they're not really "your" money anyway. The first time costs jump is if you need Supabase's paid plan — that's a sign the business is growing.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

- [ ] **Lovable** — [lovable.dev](https://lovable.dev) · Free to start building; check current pricing for the plan that allows a custom domain and removes branding. No approval wait.

- [ ] **Supabase** — [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) · Free tier is enough to build and launch. Create an account, then connect it to Lovable when prompted. No approval wait.

- [ ] **Stripe** — ✅ You already have this. Make sure your account has payouts enabled (you've completed identity verification). No new account needed.

- [ ] **Twilio** — [twilio.com](https://twilio.com)
  - Create an account (free trial gives ~$15 in credits)
  - Buy a US local phone number (~$1.15/month — verify current rate at twilio.com/pricing)
  - ⚠️ **Immediately start A2P 10DLC registration** — this registers your number as a legitimate business sender with US carriers. It is required before texting real customers at volume and takes **1–3 weeks to approve**. Don't skip this; unregistered numbers get silently blocked. Twilio walks you through it in their console.

---

## Context Carry

**Platforms:** Web app (PWA — installable via browser, not App Store), works on iPhone and Android.
**Stack:** React via Lovable (frontend) → Supabase Edge Functions (backend API) → PostgreSQL with RLS (database) → Supabase Auth (login + roles) → Supabase Storage private bucket (dog photos) → Stripe (deposits via Edge Function) → Twilio (SMS reminders via Edge Function + cron).
**Entities:** `profiles` (id, name, phone, address, role), `dogs` (id, customer_id, name, breed, notes, photo_url), `bookings` (id, customer_id, dog_id, slot_time, status, deposit_paid, stripe_payment_intent_id).
**Trust rules:** Browser holds only the Supabase `anon` key and JWT. All secret keys (Stripe, Twilio, service_role) live exclusively in Edge Function environment variables. Role stored in `profiles.role`; RLS blocks users from editing it. Dog photos in private storage, served via 1-hour expiring signed URLs only.
**ADRs 1–10:** Lovable frontend, Supabase backend, RLS for privacy, DB role storage, Stripe payments, Twilio SMS, Edge Functions for secrets, PWA not native, private storage bucket, cron scheduler.

## App Store vs. Home-Screen Web App — Read This First

**Lovable can only build web apps.** It produces a React application that runs in a browser. It cannot produce a native iPhone app, a native Android app, or a React Native (one codebase that compiles to both store apps) build. This is a hard limit of the tool, not a choice I'm making.

The alternative to a native app is a **PWA (Progressive Web App)** — a website that looks and behaves like an app, can live on the phone's home screen, and works offline for basic tasks. Here is what each path costs your users:

| | Home-screen web app (PWA) | Real App Store app |
|---|---|---|
| Found by searching the App Store? | **No** — Marisol shares a link | Yes |
| Works on iPhone + Android? | Yes | Yes |
| iPhone installation | Tap Share → "Add to Home Screen" (extra steps, easy to miss) | Tap "Get" |
| Push notifications | Android: yes. iPhone: limited — requires iOS 16.4 or later *and* the app must already be saved to home screen | Full on both |
| SMS reminders | Same either way | Same either way |
| Store fees | None | Apple: ~$99/year · Google: ~$25 one-time |
| Update speed | Instant — no review | Every release reviewed (plan for 1+ days per update, sometimes longer) |
| Payment processor cut | Stripe only (2.9 % + $0.30) | In-person services like grooming are generally exempt from Apple/Google's in-app purchase rules — verify current store policies before launch |
| Buildable with Lovable? | **Yes** | **No** |

**My recommendation: build a PWA with Lovable.** Marisol knows every customer personally — she can text them a link once. App Store discovery adds almost zero value for a local van business. SMS reminders work identically. You stay in Lovable, stay under budget, and ship in weeks instead of months.

**The honest trade-off:** customers asked for "a real app I can find in the App Store." That expectation cannot be met with Lovable. Marisol should tell customers up front: "It works like an app on your phone — I'll send you the link and you save it." If this remains a blocker after launch, the path forward is rebuilding in a different tool such as FlutterFlow or Expo, which is outside this project's scope.

Because this is a web app, the MOBILE notes in sections 1, 4, 5, and 10 are skipped.

# ARCHITECTURE.md — GroomGo

## 1. Stack Decision

> **Plain-English primer on terms used in this table:**
> - *Serverless function* — a small program that runs on someone else's server only when called; you pay per call, not per hour.
> - *Row-Level Security (RLS)* — a database feature that bakes "who can see whose rows" directly into the database itself, not just into app code. Even if app code has a bug, the database refuses to hand over the wrong data.
> - *CDN (Content Delivery Network)* — a network of servers spread around the world that serve your app's files quickly from whichever location is nearest to the user.
> - *JWT token* — a short string the auth service signs and gives to the user after login; the user presents it on every request as proof of identity, like a wristband at a concert.
> - *Environment variable* — a secret setting stored on the server itself, separate from the code — like a password kept in a locked drawer, not written on a sticky note.

| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected alternative & why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | React (Lovable-generated) | Lovable decides this — nothing to configure | — |
| Backend / API | Supabase Edge Functions (serverless TypeScript functions) | Native Lovable integration; configured entirely through a web dashboard; no terminal needed; the right place to keep secret keys away from the browser | Firebase Cloud Functions — similar concept but adds a second account and less Lovable integration |
| Database | Supabase PostgreSQL with RLS | Battle-tested relational database; RLS enforces the "customers must NEVER see other customers' data" rule at the database layer, not just in app code | PlanetScale / Neon — separate accounts, no built-in auth integration |
| Auth | Supabase Auth | Ships free with Supabase; manages login, sessions, and JWT tokens; role stored in the database where users can't touch it | Clerk / Auth0 — extra monthly cost, extra integration work |
| File storage | Supabase Storage (private bucket) | Ships with Supabase; supports expiring signed URLs (temporary links that expire after one hour) so dog photos are never permanently public | Cloudinary — generous free tier but an extra service to manage |
| Payments | Stripe Checkout (called from Edge Function) | User already has an account; Stripe hosts the payment page so raw card numbers never touch our system | PayPal — clunkier experience, harder to capture an exact $20 deposit |
| SMS / Notifications | Twilio SMS | Industry standard for automated texts; ~$0.0075 per message | AWS SNS — similar price but more setup and AWS account complexity |

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### What runs in the browser (untrusted)

The browser — including every line of JavaScript Lovable generates — is untrusted. Anyone with browser developer tools can read it, including any keys accidentally placed there.

Safe to run in the browser:
- Displaying the booking calendar, dog profile forms, and the customer's own booking list
- Calling Supabase using the **public anon key** — this is safe to expose; it's designed to be public. RLS policies, not the key, restrict what data comes back.
- Redirecting to Stripe's hosted checkout page (the browser just follows a URL; no card data or secret key passes through it)

### What must run on the server (trusted)

| Item | Location | Why it can't be in the browser |
|---|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Edge Function env var | Exposed in browser = anyone can charge cards on your account |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Edge Function env var | Used to verify Stripe's signature on each webhook; exposure allows fake payment confirmations |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Edge Function env var | Exposed in browser = anyone can send SMS on your account |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Edge Function env var | Bypasses all RLS rules entirely — the most dangerous key in the system |
| Setting `deposit_paid = true` | `stripe-webhook` Edge Function only | Must only happen after a verified server-to-server webhook from Stripe |
| Role checks (is this user the groomer?) | Supabase RLS policies in the database | If checked only in the browser, a user could modify the check in developer tools |

### Where roles are stored and who can change them

Marisol's `role = 'groomer'` is set directly in the `customers` table using the Supabase dashboard by you. The RLS UPDATE policy for `customers` explicitly excludes the `role` column — no user can change their own role, no matter what the UI does. There is no "make me a groomer" button anywhere.

### File storage

| Bucket | Contents | Public? | How files are accessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dog-photos` | Dog profile photos | **Private** | A **signed URL** — a temporary link with a secret code built in that expires after one hour — is generated by the server when a customer or groomer needs to view a photo. No photo URL is permanent or shareable without a fresh server-issued link. |

### ⚠️ Known Lovable risk

Lovable sometimes generates Supabase calls that use the service role key in the frontend code, or Stripe API calls that use the secret key in the browser. Before you go live, search the generated codebase for these strings:

- `service_role`
- `sk_live_`
- `sk_test_`

If any of those appear outside a Supabase Edge Function file, stop and move them to Edge Function environment variables before deploying.

| **Supabase** | Database, auth, storage, edge functions, cron | Anon key (in app, safe) · Service role key (private) | Service role key in Edge Function env vars only | 500 MB database · 1 GB storage · 2 GB bandwidth · 500 K function calls/month | App stops working; Supabase has 99.9 % uptime SLA on Pro; free tier has no SLA — acceptable for V1 |
| **Stripe** | $20 deposit collection | Publishable key (in app, safe) · Secret key (private) | Secret key in Edge Function env vars only | No monthly fee; 2.9 % + $0.30 per transaction | Payment page fails; add a UI message "Payment unavailable, please try again shortly"; existing bookings unaffected |
| **Twilio** | SMS reminder texts the day before appointments | Account SID (less sensitive) · Auth token (private) | Auth token in Edge Function env vars only | ~$1.50/month for a US phone number; $0.0075 per outgoing SMS | Reminders don't send; booking still exists; Marisol's day view should show a "⚠ Reminder not sent" flag so she can call manually |

**Stripe + in-person services note:** Dog grooming is an in-person physical service, not a digital product or subscription. Apple and Google generally do not require their in-app purchase systems for in-person services, which means Stripe's standard fee applies and Apple/Google take no cut. Store policies change — verify this before launch at developer.apple.com and developer.android.com.

**⚠️ A2P 10DLC — start this immediately:** In the United States, mobile carriers require businesses that send automated texts to register under a program called **A2P 10DLC** (Application-to-Person, 10-digit long code). Without it, your reminder texts will be silently filtered or blocked by carriers. Registration takes **1–4 weeks** and costs a small one-time fee (~$4–20). Start it the same day you create your Twilio account. You'll need: business name, a brief description of the app's purpose, and a sample message (e.g., "Hi [Name], reminder: your GroomGo appointment is tomorrow at 10 AM. Reply STOP to opt out.").

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

1. **ADR-1:** Use Lovable for the frontend because it is the specified build tool.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, storage, and edge functions because it integrates natively with Lovable and requires no terminal work.
3. **ADR-3:** Build a PWA (home-screen web app) instead of a native App Store app because Lovable cannot produce native apps.
4. **ADR-4:** Store all secret keys exclusively in Supabase Edge Function environment variables, never in any frontend code.
5. **ADR-5:** Enforce data isolation with Supabase RLS policies baked into the database, not only in application code, to prevent customers from ever seeing another customer's address or phone number.
6. **ADR-6:** Set `deposit_paid = true` only via the verified `stripe-webhook` Edge Function, never from the browser, to prevent fake payment confirmations.
7. **ADR-7:** Store dog photos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them via signed URLs that expire after one hour.
8. **ADR-8:** Use Twilio SMS triggered by a nightly Supabase pg_cron job for day-before reminders.
9. **ADR-9:** Snapshot the customer's address into `bookings.address_snapshot` at booking time so the groomer's route is accurate even if the customer later changes their address.
10. **ADR-10:** Set Marisol's groomer role directly in the database via the Supabase dashboard; do not expose any role-editing UI to any user.

None may appear outside Edge Function files. Make this a launch checklist item. |

Set up cron-job.org as a free fallback: it hits the same Edge Function URL on a daily schedule without needing pg_cron. |

## 9. In Plain English

- **Customer data is locked to each account at the database level.** The database itself has rules that make it physically impossible for one customer's record — including their home address — to be returned when someone else is logged in. Even a bug in the app code can't override this.
- **Marisol's special access can't be self-granted.** Her ability to see everyone's bookings and route is set directly in the database by you, not through any button in the app. A customer can't promote themselves to groomer.
- **Stripe takes payment, then tells the app.** When a customer pays, they're sent to Stripe's own payment page. Stripe then sends a private notification directly to our server to say "this worked." The app only marks the deposit as paid after receiving that notification — the customer's browser has no say in it.
- **Reminder texts happen automatically every night.** A small program inside the database runs each night, finds all appointments scheduled for the next day, and fires a text to each customer through Twilio. Marisol doesn't press anything.
- **The app lives on customers' home screens, not in the App Store.** Marisol texts customers a link. On iPhone, they tap Share → "Add to Home Screen" and it looks and works like an app. Searching the App Store won't find it — she has to share the link herself.

| `bookings` | Own bookings only / groomer: all bookings | Customer (own bookings only) | Customer: cancel own only / groomer: status updates | Nobody |

> **"Must NEVER" enforcement:** The `customers.address` and `customers.phone` fields are readable only by the owning customer and the groomer. These rules live in the database itself (RLS policies), not just in the app UI, so they cannot be bypassed by a clever API call.

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### What runs in the browser (untrusted)

Everything that runs on the user's phone is untrusted — anyone who knows what they're doing can intercept it, modify it, or read it. This includes:

- The React UI (all the screens, buttons, forms)
- Reading the logged-in user's own data via Supabase's client library
- Redirecting the customer to Stripe's hosted payment page
- Requesting a signed (expiring) URL to display a dog photo

**Nothing secret, no permission checks, no payment actions live here.**

### What runs on Supabase's servers (trusted)

- Creating a Stripe Checkout session (requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`)
- Receiving and verifying Stripe's payment webhook (requires `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`)
- Marking `deposit_paid = true` after verified payment
- Sending SMS reminders via Twilio (requires Twilio credentials)
- The daily cron job (scheduled task — like an alarm clock for code) that finds tomorrow's bookings

### ⚠️ Lovable-specific warning

Lovable sometimes generates code that calls external services (like Twilio) directly from the React frontend. **This would expose your secret keys in the browser.** Before you connect any live keys, review the generated code. Any call to Stripe or Twilio must go through an Edge Function, not a frontend file. If you see `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` or `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` appear anywhere in Lovable's frontend code, it must be moved.

### Where roles are stored

The `role` field lives in the `profiles` table in the database. A RLS policy blocks any user from updating their own `role` column. Marisol's role is set manually once in the Supabase dashboard by you. It is **not** stored in the browser, not in a cookie the user can edit, and not in any profile field the user can change through the app.

### File storage

| What | Bucket type | How accessed | Personal? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dog photos | Private | Signed URL (expiring link, valid ~1 hour, generated by Supabase Storage) | ✅ Yes — only the owning customer and the groomer can request a signed URL |

There are no public file URLs anywhere in this system. Every photo request goes through an RLS-checked signed URL call.

### Supabase keys — critical distinction

Supabase gives you two keys:
- **`anon` key** — safe to put in the frontend. RLS policies still apply.
- **`service_role` key** — bypasses ALL RLS. Goes in Edge Functions only, never in any frontend file.

---

## 5. External Services

| Service | Purpose | Which key(s) | Where key is stored | Free-tier limits | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, auth, file storage, Edge Functions | `service_role` key (server only), `anon` key (frontend) | `service_role` in Edge Function env vars; `anon` key in Lovable frontend config | Free: 500 MB database, 1 GB storage, 50,000 monthly active users, 500 MB Edge Function invocations | App is fully down — critical single dependency; Supabase has 99.9% uptime SLA on Pro |
| **Stripe** | $20 deposit checkout | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Supabase Edge Function environment variables | No monthly fee; **2.9% + $0.30 per transaction** (deducted from each $20 deposit — Marisol receives ~$19.12 per booking) | Customers cannot pay deposit; booking stays in `pending` status; you can allow undeposited bookings temporarily |
| **Twilio** | Day-before SMS reminders | `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER` | Supabase Edge Function environment variables | No free tier for production; ~$0.0079/SMS in the US; phone number ~$1/month; **A2P 10DLC registration required** (see below) | Reminders not sent; Marisol should check bookings manually that day; set up an alert in Twilio dashboard |

### A2P 10DLC — the registration that takes weeks

A2P 10DLC (Application-to-Person 10-digit long code — industry jargon for "a business texting via a regular phone number") is a US carrier requirement for any business sending automated texts. Without it, your messages will be blocked or heavily filtered. **Start this registration on day one of development.** It costs approximately $4/month for the messaging campaign fee and takes **2–4 weeks** to be approved. Twilio's dashboard walks you through the steps.

> **Stripe fees are not an operating expense.** They come out of each deposit. Every $20 paid, Stripe takes ~$0.88. Marisol keeps ~$19.12. This is revenue math, not a budget line.

> **This fits within the $50/month budget** at all realistic scales for V1.

---

## 7. Decisions Log

These are final unless you explicitly change them.

1. **ADR-1:** Use Lovable + Supabase as the full platform because it matches the build tool constraint and requires zero terminal work.
2. **ADR-2:** Run all secret-key operations (Stripe, Twilio) in Supabase Edge Functions because secrets must never appear in browser-side code.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Stripe Checkout (Stripe's hosted payment page) instead of a custom card form because it requires no PCI compliance work and is simpler to build.
4. **ADR-4:** Use Twilio for SMS reminders because it is the most documented SMS API at this price point.
5. **ADR-5:** Build as a PWA (home-screen web app) rather than a native app because Lovable cannot produce App Store apps and the budget does not support switching tools.
6. **ADR-6:** Store the user role in a `profiles` database table with an RLS policy that blocks self-update, not in browser storage or editable user metadata.
7. **ADR-7:** Store dog photos in a private Supabase Storage bucket and serve them via signed expiring links, never public URLs.
8. **ADR-8:** Enforce the "customers must NEVER see other customers' data" rule at the database layer (RLS), not only in the UI, so it cannot be bypassed.

| # | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A2P 10DLC delay blocks SMS at launch.** If registration isn't approved, all reminder texts are silently filtered by carriers. | Start the Twilio A2P registration on the first day of development. Use Twilio's trial mode (which works with verified numbers) while waiting. Plan to launch no earlier than 3 weeks after submitting registration. |
| 2 | **Lovable generates frontend code that calls Stripe or Twilio directly,** exposing secret keys in the browser. | Before connecting any live keys, search Lovable's generated code for `STRIPE_SECRET` and `TWILIO`. If found, move those calls to an Edge Function. Never paste a live secret key into Lovable's frontend environment variables. |
| 3 | **An RLS policy gap lets one customer read another's address or phone.** A single typo in a policy can open a serious privacy hole. | Before launch, create two test customer accounts. Log in as customer A and attempt to view customer B's bookings, address, and phone — both through the app and by querying Supabase directly. All attempts must return empty results or errors. |
| 4 | **Stripe webhook not verified,** allowing a bad actor to fake a "payment complete" POST and get a booking without paying. | The Edge Function that receives Stripe webhooks must always verify the request signature using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Supabase's Edge Function examples for Stripe include this step — don't skip it. |
| 5 | **Marisol gets locked out of her groomer account** and can't see the day's route. | Set a recovery email on the account. Document the Supabase password-reset URL in a note on her phone. Optionally create a second groomer login as a backup. |

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website, not an App Store app.** Customers open a link you send them, then tap "Add to Home Screen." It looks and feels like an app, but it won't show up in a search on the App Store. You tell customers: "Go to [your website] and save it to your home screen."

- **Supabase is your locked filing cabinet.** It holds every customer's name, address, and bookings, and it has built-in rules — set once, enforced forever — that mean each customer can only ever open their own drawer. There is no way for one customer to read another customer's address, even if they're technically savvy.

- **When a customer pays their deposit, they leave your app and go to Stripe's website.** Stripe handles the card, sends your app a quiet tap on the shoulder saying "payment done," and your app marks the booking as paid. You never see or store card numbers.

- **Reminder texts happen automatically overnight.** A tiny program wakes up at 9 AM every day, checks who has a booking tomorrow, and sends each of them a text through Twilio. You don't have to do anything manually.

- **Your secret passwords (for Stripe and Twilio) never leave Supabase's servers.** They are never written into the code that runs on a customer's phone, so there's nothing for anyone to steal from the app itself.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

- [ ] **Lovable** — lovable.dev. Free tier available; Pro plan needed for a custom domain and production use (~$20/month — verify current pricing). No approval required, instant signup.

- [ ] **Supabase** — supabase.com. Free tier is sufficient to start. No approval required, instant signup. Create one project and save the project URL and `anon` key for Lovable, and the `service_role` key for Edge Function environment variables (never share the service role key).

- [ ] **Stripe** ✅ — you already have this. Make sure live mode is activated (requires identity verification — usually same-day). Create a product called "Grooming Deposit" priced at $20 in the Stripe dashboard. Note your `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (starts with `sk_live_`) and set up a webhook endpoint pointing to your Edge Function — Stripe will give you a `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` when you do.

- [ ] **Twilio** — twilio.com. Sign up and purchase a local phone number (~$1/month). ⚠️ **Start A2P 10DLC registration immediately.** This is the US carrier registration required before your texts will be delivered to real customers. Estimated time: **2–4 weeks.** Cost: ~$4/month campaign fee after approval. Twilio's dashboard has a guided registration flow under "Messaging → Regulatory Compliance." Your trial account works for testing with verified numbers in the meantime.

- [ ] **One manual Supabase setup step after the app is built:** Find Marisol's user ID in the Supabase Auth dashboard and set her `profiles.role` to `'groomer'` directly in the database table editor. This is a one-time, two-minute step that gives her access to the groomer day view.

## Context Carry

**Platform:** Web app (PWA — home-screen web app, not in App Store). Runs in mobile browser on iPhone and Android.

**Stack:** Lovable (React frontend + hosting) · Supabase (PostgreSQL database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions) · Stripe Checkout ($20 deposit) · Twilio (SMS reminders).

## App-Store App vs. Web App: My Recommendation

You said you need iPhone **and** Android, and that you want Stripe to handle the $9.99/month charge so Apple and Google don't take a cut. These two goals conflict directly for native app-store apps.

**The conflict in plain English:** Apple and Google both have a rule that if you sell digital features or content (a fitness plan subscription counts) inside an app they distribute, the payment *must* go through their own system — Apple's "In-App Purchase" or Google's "Play Billing." They each keep 15–30% of every charge. An app submitted to either store that uses Stripe for subscriptions will be rejected.

**Your two real options:**

| | PWA (web app on home screen) | Native app-store app |
|---|---|---|
| Discoverable in App Store / Play Store | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Stripe payments — full $9.99 goes to you | ✅ Yes | ❌ Must use IAP; lose 15–30% |
| Install steps on iPhone | Extra — Share → "Add to Home Screen" | Normal one-tap |
| Developer fees | $0 | ~$99/yr Apple + $25 once Google |
| Delay per update you release | None — instant | 1–7 days per review |
| Push notifications | Limited — iOS 16.4+ only, and only after user adds to home screen | Full |
| Camera & video recording | ✅ Works on iOS 14.3+ in Safari; ✅ Android Chrome | ✅ Works |

**I recommend the PWA.** For a solo builder on a $75/month budget whose primary requirement is keeping all subscription revenue, the PWA wins outright. Your users lose the ability to find you by searching the app store, and iPhone users need one extra install step — but after that they use it exactly like a regular app. You keep roughly 97% of every $9.99 (Stripe takes ~$0.59 per transaction).

Expo, your build tool, supports both paths. This document follows the PWA path. The MOBILE-specific notes in the brief (sections 1, 4, 5, 10) are skipped because they apply only to app-store builds.

## 1. Stack Decision

| Backend / API | Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) | Server-side programs that run inside Supabase; keep all secret keys and AI calls off the client device; no extra server to manage or pay for | Separate Node.js server on Railway or Render — another service, another bill, another failure point |
| Database | Supabase PostgreSQL | You already have an account; ships with Row-Level Security — RLS means database rules live *inside* the database itself, so even a buggy query returns only the rows the logged-in user is allowed to see; included in the free plan | PlanetScale or Neon — both solid, but redundant when Supabase already provides it |

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### What runs in the browser — untrusted

The browser (and the PWA running inside it) is untrusted. Users control this environment. Anyone with developer tools can read whatever is in the JavaScript bundle, browser storage, or memory.

**Safe to run in the browser:**
- All UI screens, forms, charts
- Reading Supabase data via the Supabase JS library with the user's JWT — safe because RLS rejects unauthorized reads at the database level regardless of what the browser sends
- Uploading videos directly to Supabase Storage with the user's JWT — the storage bucket's RLS rejects uploads to paths that aren't owned by that user
- Stripe.js — Stripe's own client script that handles card input; card data goes straight to Stripe's servers and never touches your code
- Displaying AI feedback once it has been written to the database

**Must never ship in the browser:**

| Secret / action | Why it must stay server-side |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Creates checkout sessions and verifies webhooks; anyone with it can move money on your behalf |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Anyone with it can run up your AI bill |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Anyone with it can send email as you |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Verifies that Stripe — not an impersonator — sent the payment event |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Bypasses all RLS; would let anyone read any row in your database |
| Creating or canceling subscriptions | Must confirm payment server-side before granting access |
| Calling Gemini | Secret key protection + cost control |
| Assigning or changing roles | Must be a trusted server action, never user-submitted |
| Generating signed URLs for videos | Must verify the requester owns the video before issuing the link |

**What is safe to put in the browser:**
- `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — these identify your project but grant no special access; RLS does all the gatekeeping
- `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` — Stripe's public identifier; designed to be in the browser

> ⚠️ **Supabase Edge Functions pitfall:** Supabase lets you access secrets through `Deno.env.get()` inside Edge Functions. Make sure the `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and all API keys are set only in the Supabase dashboard under "Edge Function Secrets," never in `.env` files committed to your repository.

### Where roles are stored and who can change them

Roles live in the `user_roles` table in PostgreSQL. The RLS policy on this table is:

- **SELECT:** a user may read only their own row
- **INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE:** only the `service_role` key (held exclusively by Edge Functions) may write

This means no user — regardless of what they send to the API — can change their own role. There is no profile form, no API route, no URL that accepts a role change from a client. A new account is assigned `'member'` by an Edge Function at registration. You set your own account to `'coach'` once during initial setup by running a direct Edge Function call with the service role key.

### File storage

| Bucket | Contents | Public | How members access it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `form-videos` | All member workout videos | ❌ Private | Time-limited signed URL from an Edge Function; expires after 1 hour |

There are no public buckets in V1. Any request to download a video without a valid, unexpired signed URL returns a 403 error from Supabase Storage.

**Signed URL flow:**
1. Member opens their video in the app
2. App calls an Edge Function: "I want a link to video `{id}`"
3. Edge Function checks `form_videos.member_id = auth.uid()` — if it doesn't match, it returns a 403
4. Edge Function generates a 1-hour signed URL using the service role key
5. App streams or plays the video directly from that URL
6. One hour later the URL is dead; no permanent link exists

## 7. Decisions Log

1. **ADR-1:** Use PWA over native app-store apps because Stripe subscriptions are incompatible with Apple and Google in-app purchase requirements.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase for database, auth, and storage because the builder already has an account and it covers all three needs in one managed platform.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Edge Functions for all server-side logic because it keeps secrets and AI calls on the same platform as the database with no extra infrastructure.
4. **ADR-4:** Use Google Gemini 2.0 Flash for video analysis because it accepts raw video natively and costs roughly 10× less than GPT-4o Vision for this use case.
5. **ADR-5:** Use a private Supabase Storage bucket with Edge-Function-generated signed URLs for all form videos because members must never access each other's files.
6. **ADR-6:** Store roles in a dedicated `user_roles` table writable only by `service_role` because users must not be able to promote themselves to coach.
7. **ADR-7:** Use Stripe hosted checkout (redirect to Stripe's own payment page) rather than embedding card fields, because card data never touches our servers.
8. **ADR-8:** Use Vercel for PWA hosting because it's free at launch and deploys directly from Expo's web export output.
9. **ADR-9:** Enforce a 30-day video retention policy via a scheduled Edge Function to keep Supabase Storage within the Pro plan's 100 GB limit at scale.
10. **ADR-10:** Use Resend for transactional email because it offers 3,000 free emails/month and a single API call from Edge Functions.

## 8. Known Risks

| # | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Gemini is unavailable when a member submits a video** | Write `feedback_status = 'pending'` immediately on upload. A scheduled Edge Function runs every 10 minutes to retry any rows in `'pending'` or `'error'` state. The member sees "Feedback on the way — check back in a few minutes" instead of an error screen. The rest of the app is unaffected. |
| 2 | **Stripe webhook arrives late, out of order, or duplicated** | Stripe retries failed webhooks for 72 hours. The Edge Function processing webhooks is idempotent — a technical term meaning running it twice produces the same result as running it once. It checks `stripe_subscription_id` before writing, so duplicate events cause no harm. |
| 3 | **Video storage costs spike as users accumulate recordings** | The 30-day retention policy (ADR-9) caps total storage. A scheduled Edge Function deletes old rows from `form_videos` and the corresponding files from the Storage bucket. Set a Supabase dashboard alert when storage exceeds 80 GB; upgrade or tighten retention before hitting 100 GB. |
| 4 | **A bug in an Edge Function issues a signed URL for the wrong member's video** | Two independent checks must both fail simultaneously for a leak: (1) the Edge Function queries `form_videos WHERE id = ? AND member_id = auth.uid()` and returns 403 if that check fails; (2) the storage path is structured as `{member_id}/{video_id}` so a URL for member A's path simply won't work for member B even if somehow issued. |
| 5 | **iPhone users don't know how to install a PWA** | Show a dismissible "Install this app" banner the first time an iPhone user visits in Safari, with a three-step screenshot (Share icon → scroll down → "Add to Home Screen"). This is a conversion problem, not a technical one, but it affects your signup rate and deserves a clear onboarding screen before launch. |

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website that acts like an app.** It lives at your own domain (e.g., `formcoach.app`). Members tap a link, add it to their phone's home screen, and from then on it works just like any other app icon — with no App Store involved. Because of this, every $9.99 goes to your Stripe account minus a small card-processing fee (about 59 cents per transaction). Apple and Google get nothing.

- **Supabase is your engine room.** It stores all your data, handles logins, keeps videos locked in a private file cabinet, and runs small server programs that do the sensitive work — like processing payments and asking the AI for feedback. You already have an account and it costs nothing until you have enough users to care.

- **Every member's body measurements and workout videos are invisible to everyone else.** This isn't just a UI feature — it's enforced inside the database itself. Even if someone sent a hand-crafted request trying to read another member's data, the database would refuse before any code runs. Videos can only be played through a link that expires after one hour, generated by your server only after confirming it's that member's own video.

- **Stripe takes care of all the money.** When someone clicks "Subscribe," they're sent to a Stripe-hosted payment page — like walking to a separate cashier. Their card number never passes through your app. Once they pay, Stripe sends a private signal to your server, which then unlocks their access. Your app just waits for that signal rather than trusting anything the browser tells it.

- **Your costs start near zero and grow slowly.** You'll pay nothing meaningful until you have 30–40 active users uploading videos (that's when you'll need Supabase's $25/month paid plan for extra storage). Everything else — hosting, email, AI analysis — stays at or near free until you're well past 100 paying members. At 1,000 users your infrastructure bill is under $60/month while your revenue is close to $6,000/month.

## App Store vs. Home-Screen Web App — Read This First

Your spec includes two hard constraints that are in direct tension: **Stripe payments without Apple or Google taking a cut**, and **runs on iPhone and Android**. Here is what you need to know before reading a single line of architecture.

**Option A — App Store + Google Play (native app)**
Both stores require you to use their in-app purchase (IAP — the stores' own payment system built into the phone) for digital subscriptions. Apple takes 15–30%; Google takes 15–30%. Your $9.99 becomes roughly $6.99–$8.49 after their cut. You cannot legally offer Stripe as an alternative inside a store app without risking rejection or removal. Every code change also goes through store review, which can take a day or more per release. Apple Developer Program is ~$99/year; Google Play Console is ~$25 one-time.

**Option B — PWA (Progressive Web App — a website users add to their home screen)**
No stores involved. Stripe takes its standard ~2.9% + 30¢ per transaction. You keep ~$9.40 of every $9.99. What your users give up: they cannot find FormCoach in the App Store or Google Play; on iPhone they must open Safari, visit your URL, tap Share, then tap "Add to Home Screen" (not obvious — three steps); on Android Chrome will offer an install banner automatically; push notifications are more limited (requires iOS 16.4+ and the app must already be added to home screen). Video recording works in modern mobile browsers but has quirks on iPhone Safari that need early testing.

**My recommendation: build a PWA.** Your business model requires Stripe. This is the only clean legal path. Expo — your stated build tool — supports web/PWA export. Your users lose discoverability but gain a lower price (or better margins for you). If you hit 1,000 members and decide an app-store version is worth the IAP cut, the same Expo codebase can be adapted. For V1, PWA is correct.

Because this is a web app, the MOBILE-specific notes are skipped throughout.

### ACCESS RULES

These rules are implemented as Row Level Security (RLS) policies — rules enforced by the database engine itself, not just your app code. Even if there is a bug in the app, the database refuses to return data that violates these rules.

| Entity | Member READ | Member CREATE | Member UPDATE | Member DELETE | Coach READ | Coach CREATE | Coach UPDATE | Coach DELETE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| members | **Own row only** | System only (Auth trigger on sign-up) | Own row — **`role` field blocked by policy** | Never | All rows | Never | Any row including `role` | Never |
| plan_templates | Templates assigned to them only | Never | Never | Never | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| template_exercises | From their assigned template only | Never | Never | Never | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| member_plans | Own rows | Never | Never | Never | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| workouts | Own rows | Never | Own rows: `completed_at` only | Never | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| sets | **Own rows only** | Own workouts | Own rows | Own rows | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **form_videos** | **OWN rows ONLY — enforced at database level, not just app code** | Own (active subscription required) | Edge Function only (status + feedback via service key) | Never | All | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| subscriptions | Own row — `status` and `current_period_end` only | Edge Function only | Edge Function only | Edge Function only | All | No | No | No |

---

## 4. Trust Boundaries

### Untrusted — the browser / phone screen
The PWA runs inside the user's phone browser. Anyone with basic technical knowledge can open developer tools, read all the JavaScript, and see everything stored there. Treat it like a public notice board.

**What lives here and why it is safe:**
- **Supabase anon key** — a public key. Every request made with it still passes through RLS. The database's own rules limit what it can return. This key being visible is by design.
- **Stripe publishable key** — a public key. It can only initiate a payment flow on a Stripe-hosted page. It cannot charge a card.

**What must never be here:** every secret key (see below).

### Trusted — Supabase Edge Functions
These run on Supabase's servers, not in the user's browser. They are the only place secrets live.

| Secret | Why it must stay here |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Creates charges and payment sessions. If exposed, anyone can bill your customers |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Proves a webhook message (the automated notification Stripe sends when a payment succeeds) genuinely came from Stripe and not from someone faking it |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Billed per use. If exposed, anyone can use your quota and run up your bill |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Bypasses every RLS rule. If exposed, anyone can read every member's private data |

**Where role is stored:** The `role` column lives in the `members` table in PostgreSQL. An RLS policy explicitly blocks any member from running `UPDATE members SET role = 'coach'` on their own row. Role can only be set by you directly in the Supabase dashboard, or by an Edge Function using the service role key. It is **not** stored in browser local storage, session storage, or any editable profile metadata.

**File storage:** All videos and frames are in a **private** Supabase Storage bucket. No file has a public URL — ever. Access is only via signed URLs generated by the backend on demand, with a short expiry (15–60 minutes). When a member requests a signed URL, the RLS policy confirms the file belongs to them before the URL is generated. A member cannot get a URL for another member's file.

**Critical Expo gotcha:** Expo uses a `.env` file and `app.config.js` to set environment variables. Any variable you prefix with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` is bundled into the JavaScript that ships to users and is visible to anyone who inspects the app. Only two variables belong there:

```
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=...
EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=...
```

Everything else — Stripe secret, OpenAI key, service role key — goes into **Supabase Edge Function secrets** (set in the Supabase dashboard under Edge Functions → Secrets). They never touch the Expo project.

## 7. Decisions Log

1. **ADR-1:** Use PWA (Expo Web) instead of native app-store apps because the business model requires Stripe direct billing and both major stores mandate their own payment system for digital subscriptions.
2. **ADR-2:** Use Supabase as the sole back-end platform (database, auth, storage, edge functions) because the user already has an account and it covers all server-side needs without a second service.
3. **ADR-3:** Use Supabase Row Level Security as the primary privacy layer between members, not application-level code alone, because database-enforced rules hold even when there is a bug in the app.
4. **ADR-4:** Store the `role` field in the `members` table protected by RLS, not in Supabase Auth user metadata (which members can edit), because members must never be able to promote themselves to coach.
5. **ADR-5:** Extract video frames client-side using the browser's canvas API and upload them as JPEG images, avoiding server-side video processing tools (like ffmpeg) that add complexity.
6. **ADR-6:** Store all videos and frames in a private Supabase Storage bucket; serve access only via short-lived signed URLs generated by the back end.
7. **ADR-7:** Delete raw video files and frame images from storage after AI feedback is saved to the database; retain only the feedback text long-term.
8. **ADR-8:** Use Stripe Checkout (Stripe's own hosted payment page), with the session created server-side, so no card data ever passes through FormCoach code.
9. **ADR-9:** Handle all Stripe subscription state changes via webhooks received by an Edge Function, not by trusting the client-side redirect after payment.
10. **ADR-10:** Host the compiled PWA on Vercel free tier, deployed automatically from a GitHub repository on every push.

| 2 | **AI form feedback quality is unpredictable.** GPT-4o can produce generic, vague, or incorrect feedback from still images. A member could follow bad advice. | Label all AI feedback clearly in the UI as "AI suggestion — not a substitute for a qualified coach or physiotherapist." Add a thumbs up / thumbs down reaction button to collect quality signals. Improve your prompts iteratively using real feedback. |
| 3 | **OpenAI bill spike.** A bug in the app, a suddenly popular post, or a bad actor could trigger many more form checks than expected, running up an unexpected invoice. | Set a monthly spending cap in your OpenAI account dashboard the day you sign up (suggest $30–50 to start). Rate-limit form checks in the Edge Function — for example, a maximum of 2 per member per calendar day. |
| 4 | **Stripe webhook missed or delayed, leaving a paying member locked out.** Network issues mean webhooks sometimes arrive late or not at all. | Handle multiple Stripe events — not just `checkout.session.completed` but also `customer.subscription.updated` and `invoice.payment_succeeded`. Add a "Restore access" button in the app that calls an Edge Function to re-check subscription status directly with Stripe in real time. |
| 5 | **Supabase free-tier limits hit unexpectedly.** 500K Edge Function calls/month sounds large but frequent polling (repeatedly asking "has anything changed?") can consume it fast. | Replace polling with Supabase Realtime subscriptions (a push-based system where the server notifies the app when something changes, instead of the app constantly asking). Monitor usage in the Supabase dashboard. Budget $25/month for the Pro plan once you have ~20 paying members — their subscription revenue covers it many times over by then. |

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website that behaves like an app.** Users visit it in their phone browser and add it to their home screen. There is no App Store involved, which means your $9.99 goes through Stripe, not Apple or Google.
- **Almost everything important happens on Supabase's computers, not the user's phone.** The phone just draws the screen. Charging cards, analysing form videos, and enforcing who can see what all happen in a secure place you control, where your secret codes live.
- **The database itself enforces privacy rules, like a bouncer who checks IDs at the door.** You don't just rely on the app to "not show" one member's videos to another — the database literally refuses to hand over that data, even if the app has a bug.
- **Videos are deleted the moment the AI is done with them.** Only the written feedback is kept. This saves money on storage and limits how long sensitive footage of members' bodies sits around.
- **Your AI costs grow with your users, but so does your revenue.** At 100 paying members you earn roughly $940 per month after Stripe fees, and spend maybe $12 on AI. By 1,000 members you are earning ~$9,400 and spending ~$90–120 on AI — a very healthy ratio.

**No Apple Developer Program and no Google Play Console needed.** You are shipping a PWA, not a native app. This saves you ~$99/year in Apple fees and removes store-review delays from every update you ship — you push to GitHub and Vercel deploys in about a minute.

# ARCHITECTURE.md — FormCoach

---

## ⚠️ App Store vs. Web App — Read This Before Anything Else

Your spec says you want Stripe so Apple and Google don't take a cut. That single requirement is the deciding factor.

**Apple's App Store rules (rule 3.1.1) require that any iOS app selling a digital subscription — access to app features, exactly like FormCoach's $9.99 plan — must use Apple's own payment system (In-App Purchase).** You cannot substitute Stripe. Violating this causes the app to be rejected in review. Apple takes 30% in year one, 15% from year two onward for subscriptions.

Google Play has a parallel policy for digital content sold inside Play Store apps.

**Expo can build both native app-store apps and web apps.** I am recommending the web path — not because Expo can't make a native app, but because the native path contradicts your payment goal.

**Recommendation: build a Progressive Web App (PWA).** A PWA is a website that members open in their phone's browser and then add to their home screen, where it looks and launches like a normal app — no app store involved, so Stripe works without restriction.

---

**What your members give up with the PWA:**

| What | Detail |
|---|---|
| App store discovery | The app does not appear in the App Store or Google Play. Members find it via a direct link or your marketing. |
| iPhone install flow | Members must open Safari, navigate to the URL, tap the Share icon, then "Add to Home Screen" — roughly three extra steps. Android Chrome shows an install banner automatically. |
| Push notifications | On iPhone, they require iOS 16.4 or later *and* the PWA must already be added to the home screen first. |
| Embedded video recorder | On iPhone, tapping Record opens the native camera app; the member records and returns. It works — it just feels slightly less seamless than a fully embedded recorder inside a native app. |

**What you give up if you chose an App Store app instead:**

- You would be forced to use Apple IAP (15–30% cut) — directly contradicting your Stripe goal.
- Every release goes through app store review, typically a day or more delay.
- Apple Developer Program: approximately $99/year. Google Play Console: approximately $25 one-time. *(Verify current fees at developer.apple.com and play.google.com/console — these change.)*

---

## 1. Stack Decision

A **layer** here means one responsibility in the system (the part that shows the screen, the part that stores data, etc.). Each choice is final per the ADR list in §7.

| Layer| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected alternative & why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | Expo (React Native for Web), exported as a PWA | You already know Expo; one codebase runs in every mobile browser. | Next.js — also valid but a second framework to learn. |
| **Backend / API** | Supabase Edge Functions — small JavaScript functions that run on demand in the cloud, no server to manage | Bundled with Supabase (which you already have); no separate server bill. | Express.js on a VPS — requires a server running 24/7, over budget at low user counts. |
| **Database** | Supabase PostgreSQL with Row Level Security (RLS — rules baked into the database that decide who can read each row, enforced even if your app code has a bug) | Already in your account; RLS is the safest way to enforce "members never see each other's data." | Firebase Firestore — weaker row-level control, harder to model relational data like sets and exercises. |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth | Built into Supabase; handles email/password and produces JWTs (tamper-proof tokens that prove who the user is) automatically. | Auth0 — adds cost and another account for no extra benefit here. |
| **File storage** | Supabase Storage, private bucket | Already in your account; supports signed expiring URLs — temporary links that die after an hour, the only safe way a member views their own video. | AWS S3 — same capability, separate account, separate billing, more setup. |
| **Payments** | Stripe Checkout + Stripe Billing + webhooks (automatic notifications Stripe sends your server when a payment event occurs) | You already have an account; hosted checkout means you never touch raw card numbers; webhook verification keeps the server in control of what gets unlocked. | Paddle — less documentation, less familiar. |
| **AI / LLM** | Google Gemini 1.5 Flash (a large language model with vision — it can watch a video and respond to a prompt) | Accepts a raw video file directly via the Files API; very generous free tier; significantly cheaper per call than GPT-4o for video input. | OpenAI GPT-4o — requires manually extracting frames before sending; more expensive at this use pattern. |
| **Hosting** | Vercel (serves your static web files globally over HTTPS) | Free tier handles early traffic; one-command deploy; HTTPS certificate automatic — required for PWA install on iPhone. | Netlify — also fine; Vercel's Expo integration is slightly smoother. |
| **Email** | Resend (transactional email — automated messages like "Welcome" or "Payment failed") | 3,000 emails/month free; fast domain verification; simple API. | SendGrid — smaller free tier, more involved signup. |
