## 4. Trust Boundaries

**Untrusted — the phone browser. Treat it as if an attacker controls it.**
- Renders the UI
- Records video and uploads it via a short-lived signed URL the server generates
- Reads database rows that RLS has already filtered to the logged-in member's own data
- Sends requests to Edge Functions
- Holds **zero** secret API keys

**Trusted — Supabase Edge Functions. This is your server.**
- Holds all secret keys: Stripe secret key, Stripe webhook signing secret, Gemini API key, Supabase service-role key
- Creates Stripe Checkout sessions
- Verifies every incoming Stripe webhook signature before trusting the payment event
- Downloads videos from Storage and uploads them to Gemini's Files API
- Generates signed 1-hour-expiring URLs for video playback
- Updates subscription status
- Generates Stripe Customer Portal session URLs so members can cancel or update their card

**Where role is stored and how it is locked:**
`members.role` in PostgreSQL. It defaults to `'member'` on signup via a database trigger. A second trigger — `prevent_role_escalation` — fires on every UPDATE to the `members` table: if the `role` column is being changed and the request is not coming from the service-role key, the trigger raises an error and blocks the write. No normal API call from the browser can promote a member to coach. The coach assigns roles only via the Supabase dashboard or a dedicated Edge Function called with the service-role key.

**Where login tokens live:**
The Supabase JavaScript client stores the JWT in the browser's `localStorage`. This is standard for web apps. The token expires automatically (Supabase default: 1 hour, silently refreshed in the background). It is never stored in an editable profile field or read from a URL parameter.

**Stripe keys in the browser:**
The Stripe *publishable* key (starts `pk_live_…`) is safe to include in the frontend — it can only open a Checkout session, not charge a card or read your Stripe account. The Stripe *secret* key (`sk_live_…`) and webhook signing secret live only in Supabase Edge Function environment variables, set via `supabase secrets set`.

**File storage summary:**

| Bucket | Public? | How a member watches their own video |
|---|---|---|
| `form-videos` | **Private — never public** | Edge Function generates a signed URL valid for 1 hour; the URL is not stored in the database |

If a member somehow shared their signed URL with another member, it would return a 403 error after one hour. Video files are never accessible via a permanent URL.

---

## 5. External Services

| Service | Purpose | Key(s) | Stored where | Free-tier limit | If it goes down |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | Database, auth, storage, edge functions | `anon` key (public, in Vercel build env); `service_role` key (secret, never in browser) | Anon key in Vercel; service-role in Supabase secrets | Free: 500 MB DB, 1 GB storage, 2 GB bandwidth, 500 K function calls/month | App fully down. Pro tier adds a 99.9% uptime SLA. |
| **Stripe** | $9.99/month subscription billing | Publishable key (in app); secret key + webhook secret (Edge Function only) | Publishable key in Vercel build env; others in Supabase secrets | No monthly fee; 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction | New subscriptions can't start. Existing subscribers keep access — their status is already cached in your DB. |
| **Google Gemini 1.5 Flash** | AI form feedback from video | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Supabase Edge Function secrets | 1 M tokens/day, 15 req/min (free tier) | Feedback status stays `pending`. Edge Function retries up to 3 times with exponential back-off (waiting progressively longer between attempts). Member sees "Analysis in progress — check back soon." |
| **Vercel** | Hosts the PWA static files | Deploy token (CI only) | GitHub Actions secret | 100 GB bandwidth/month, unlimited deploys | App unavailable to new visitors. Cached browser sessions may still work briefly. |
| **Resend** | Transactional email: welcome, receipt, payment-failed notice | `RESEND_API_KEY` | Supabase Edge Function secrets | 3,000 emails/month free | Emails fail silently. Workouts, set logging, and AI feedback are unaffected. |

**Gemini video analysis detail:** The Edge Function (1) generates a signed read URL for the video in Supabase Storage, (2) downloads the file, (3) uploads it to Gemini's Files API, (4) sends a prompt referencing the uploaded file, (5) receives the feedback text, and (6) deletes the file from Gemini (Gemini auto-deletes after 48 hours regardless). The 10-second phone video is well under Gemini's 2 GB file limit.

**Stripe events the Edge Function must handle:**
`checkout.session.completed` · `customer.subscription.updated` · `customer.subscription.deleted` · `invoice.payment_succeeded` · `invoice.payment_failed`

**Stripe Customer Portal:** When a member clicks "Manage Subscription," the Edge Function generates a Stripe-hosted portal session URL. Stripe's page handles cancellation and card updates — no custom UI needed.

**In-app purchase note:** Because FormCoach is a PWA and not an App Store app, Apple and Google's in-app purchase requirements **do not apply**. Stripe is fully legal here. If you ever publish a native app to the App Store, this architecture must be revisited — Apple will require IAP for the subscription.

---

## 6. Cost at 0 / 100 / 1,000 Users

"Users" = paying subscribers. Stripe fees come out of revenue, not your pocket directly.

| Item | 0 users | 100 users | 1,000 users |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supabase | $0 (free) | $25/mo (Pro — storage + bandwidth) | $25 + ~$5 storage add-on |
| Vercel | $0 | $0 | $20/mo (Pro if bandwidth exceeded) |
| Google Gemini | $0 | ~$2/mo | ~$15/mo |
| Resend | $0 | $0 (well under 3 K/mo) | $20/mo (paid tier) |
| Domain name | ~$1/mo | ~$1/mo | ~$1/mo |
| **Infrastructure total** | **~$1/mo** | **~$28/mo ✅** | **~$61/mo ✅** |
| Stripe fees (from revenue) | $0 | ~$59/mo | ~$590/mo |
| **Monthly revenue** | $0 | ~$999 | ~$9,990 |

At 100 users, infrastructure comfortably fits inside your $75 budget. At 1,000 users the infrastructure is ~$61/month against ~$10K revenue — Stripe's cut becomes the real cost of doing business, but that is a good problem.

**Video storage note:** At 100 users uploading one ~15 MB video per workout session (4×/week), storage grows by roughly 2–3 GB/month. Implement a 90-day auto-delete rule on video *files* (keep the AI feedback text forever) to hold storage under 10 GB indefinitely.

---

## 7. Decisions Log

ADRs (Architectural Decision Records — one-line notes explaining why each major technical choice was made). These are final unless you explicitly change them.

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| ADR-1 | Build as a PWA, not a native app-store app, because the Stripe-direct billing requirement is incompatible with App Store digital-subscription rules. |
| ADR-2 | Use Supabase for database, auth, storage, and Edge Functions because it covers all backend needs in one service the user already has, keeping moving parts low. |
| ADR-3 | Use Supabase Row Level Security to enforce data isolation because it prevents cross-member data access at the database layer, independent of application code. |
| ADR-4 | Use Google Gemini 1.5 Flash for AI form feedback because it accepts raw video files natively, has a generous free tier, and costs less per call than GPT-4o for video. |
| ADR-5 | Use Stripe Checkout (hosted payment page) so the app never handles raw card numbers and payment compliance burden is minimized. |
| ADR-6 | Store member role only in `members.role` in PostgreSQL, protected by a database trigger, so no client-side code or API call can self-promote a member to coach. |
| ADR-7 | Store all form videos in a private Supabase Storage bucket; serve them only via signed 1-hour-expiring URLs generated by Edge Functions, so members can never access each other's videos. |
| ADR-8 | Keep all secret keys exclusively in Supabase Edge Function environment variables; no secret key appears in the frontend bundle, the database, or any log. |
| ADR-9 | Process AI video feedback asynchronously; use Supabase Realtime (a feature that pushes database row changes to connected browsers instantly) to deliver the result without polling. |
| ADR-10 | Apply a 90-day auto-delete rule to video files in Storage; keep AI feedback text and metadata forever, to control storage cost at scale. |

---

## 8. Known Risks

| # | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **iPhone camera UX** — iOS Safari opens the native camera app instead of an embedded recorder, which can confuse first-time users. | Add clear in-app copy: "Tap Record → your camera opens → record 10 seconds → tap Done to return." This is a known PWA limitation on iPhone; it is manageable with good instructions. |
| 2 | **AI feedback quality** — Gemini may produce vague or inaccurate form advice from a short phone video, especially in low light or at an unusual angle, eroding member trust. | Write a careful prompt with specific exercise names and cues. Add a disclaimer: "AI feedback is a guide — always check with a qualified coach." Log every prompt and response for your first 100 analyses so you can iterate on the prompt before word spreads. |
| 3 | **Stripe webhook missed** — if the Edge Function crashes before writing the subscription status to the database, a paid member could be locked out. | Enable Stripe's automatic webhook retries (up to 3 days by default). Write the Edge Function to be idempotent — safe to run twice with the same result — by checking for a duplicate `stripe_subscription_id` before inserting. |
| 4 | **Supabase free-tier surprise** — hitting a bandwidth or storage limit takes the app down without warning during early growth. | Set a Supabase billing alert at $0. Upgrade to Pro ($25/mo) the moment you have one paying subscriber — the first month's subscription revenue covers it. |
| 5 | **RLS misconfiguration** — a single typo in a Row Level Security policy could expose one member's data to another. | Test with two separate real browser sessions (two test accounts) before launch. Use Supabase's built-in Policy Tester. Run a manual "can account A fetch account B's video URL?" check as part of pre-launch QA. |

---

## 9. In Plain English

- **Your app is a website that feels like an app.** Members open it in their phone's browser and add it to their home screen. There is no App Store, no review process, and no Apple or Google taking a cut of your $9.99.
- **The database itself enforces privacy.** Rules baked into PostgreSQL — not just your code — make it physically impossible for one member to read another member's workout videos or body measurements, even if a bug slips into the app.
- **Payments go through a Stripe-designed page.** When a member subscribes, they leave your app briefly, pay on Stripe's page, and come back. You never see or store card numbers.
- **The AI form check happens quietly in the background.** The member uploads their video and keeps logging sets. A couple of minutes later, the feedback appears automatically in the app — similar to receiving a message — without them needing to refresh or wait on a loading screen.
- **Every sensitive operation lives on a server you never see.** The app on the phone only knows how to display things and send requests. Stripe keys, Gemini keys, payment confirmations, and video access all happen on Supabase's servers, invisible to the phone.

---

## 10. Accounts to Set Up Before Building

| Account | Cost | Notes / Lead time |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ **Supabase** | Free → Pro $25/mo | Already have. Upgrade to Pro when your first subscriber pays. |
| ✅ **Stripe** | 2.9% + $0.30/transaction | Already have. Enable Stripe Billing and Stripe Customer Portal in the dashboard before build. Takes ~10 minutes. |
| ☐ **Google AI Studio** (Gemini API) | Free up to 1 M tokens/day; pay-as-you-go after | Sign up at aistudio.google.com. Create an API key. Add a credit card for above-free-tier usage. ~5 minutes. |
| ☐ **Vercel** | Free → Pro $20/mo | Sign up at vercel.com with your GitHub account. Free tier is sufficient for launch. ~5 minutes. |
| ☐ **Resend** | Free (3,000 emails/mo) → $20/mo | Sign up at resend.com. You must verify a custom domain by adding a DNS record — DNS changes can take up to **24 hours** to propagate. Set this up the same day you buy your domain. |
| ☐ **Domain name** | ~$10–15/year | Buy from Cloudflare Registrar or Namecheap. Required for HTTPS (which iPhones require for PWA install) and for Resend domain verification. Vercel handles the HTTPS certificate automatically once you point the domain at it. |

**No Apple Developer Program or Google Play Console is needed** — this is a PWA.

**Pre-launch checklist (do before writing a single feature):**
- [ ] Point domain at Vercel and confirm HTTPS is working
- [ ] Verify custom domain in Resend (DNS — allow 24 h)
- [ ] Set Stripe webhook endpoint to your Supabase Edge Function URL
- [ ] Add all secrets to Supabase Edge Function environment via `supabase secrets set`
- [ ] Enable Supabase Realtime on the `form_videos` table
- [ ] Write two test member accounts and confirm neither can read the other's data

---

## Context Carry

**Platforms:** PWA — iPhone + Android, browser-based, no app stores.
**Stack:** Expo web export → Vercel; Supabase (PostgreSQL + RLS, Auth, private Storage, Edge Functions); Stripe Checkout + Billing; Google Gemini 1.5 Flash (async, Files API); Resend email.
**Entities:** members (sensitive: weight\_kg, measurements), measurement\_logs, plan\_templates, member\_plans, exercises, workouts, workout\_exercises, logged\_sets, form\_videos, subscriptions.
**Trust rules:** All secrets in Edge Function env vars only. Role stored in `members.role`, locked by DB trigger — no client can self-promote. Videos in private bucket, served via 1-hour signed URLs from Edge Functions only. RLS enforces cross-member isolation at DB layer. 90-day video-file auto-delete.
**ADRs:** PWA (IAP conflict); Supabase all-in-one; RLS for isolation; Gemini Flash for video AI; Stripe Checkout; role trigger-locked; private bucket + signed URLs; async feedback via Realtime; 90-day video retention.

         Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_ANON_KEY')!,

     Return 403 { error: 'Not found' } if video is null.

- [ ] **S-15 — RevenueCat webhook → subscriptions table**

  **Goal:** When Apple/Google confirm a purchase or expiry, the server-side subscriptions table is updated automatically so the Edge Function check is always accurate.

  **Build prompt:**
  ```
  Create supabase/functions/rc-webhook/index.ts.

  This function receives POST requests from RevenueCat (not from the app).

  1. Read the secret from headers:
       const authHeader = req.headers.get('Authorization') ?? '';
       const secret = Deno.env.get('RC_WEBHOOK_SECRET');
       if (authHeader !== `Bearer ${secret}`) {
         return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
       }

  2. Parse body: const event = (await req.json()).event

  3. Relevant fields:
       event.type              — e.g. 'INITIAL_PURCHASE', 'RENEWAL', 'CANCELLATION', 'EXPIRATION'
       event.app_user_id       — the Supabase user UUID (set when RevenueCat is configured)
       event.expiration_at_ms  — Unix milliseconds, may be null

  4. Create adminClient using SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from Deno.env.

  5. Handle events:
     if (['INITIAL_PURCHASE', 'RENEWAL'].includes(event.type)) {
       await adminClient.from('subscriptions').upsert({
         member_id:  event.app_user_id,
         status:     'active',
         expires_at: event.expiration_at_ms
                       ? new Date(event.expiration_at_ms).toISOString()
                       : null,
         updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
       }, { onConflict: 'member_id' });
     } else if (['CANCELLATION', 'EXPIRATION'].includes(event.type)) {
       await adminClient.from('subscriptions')
         .update({ status: 'expired', updated_at: new Date().toISOString() })
         .eq('member_id', event.app_user_id);
     }

  6. Return 200 OK.

  Deploy:
    supabase functions deploy rc-webhook
    supabase secrets set RC_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<a strong random string you generate>

  In RevenueCat dashboard → Project Settings → Webhooks → Add endpoint:
    URL: https://<your-project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/rc-webhook
    Authorization header: Bearer <RC_WEBHOOK_SECRET>
  ```

### S2.1 — Supabase schema + RLS

- [ ] **S2.1 Supabase database schema and Row-Level Security**

**Goal:** Create all database tables and enforce the privacy rules from the spec using Row-Level Security (RLS — a database feature that adds a filter to every query so a user can only see their own rows, even if their code accidentally asks for someone else's).

**Build prompt:**

> In the Supabase dashboard (https://app.supabase.com), create a new project named `formcoach-prod`. Choose a region close to your users.
>
> Once the project is created, open the SQL Editor and run the entire block below in one execution:
>
> ```sql
> -- Enable UUID generation
> create extension if not exists "uuid-ossp";
>
> ---------- ROLES ----------
> -- Role is stored server-side. App code reads it only via a server function.
> create table public.member_roles (
>   user_id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
>   role    text not null check (role in ('member', 'coach'))
> );
> alter table public.member_roles enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own role"
>   on public.member_roles for select
>   using (auth.uid() = user_id);
> -- No insert/update policy: role is written by a server function only.
>
> ---------- MEMBERS ----------
> create table public.members (
>   id           uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
>   email        text not null,
>   display_name text,
>   weight_kg    numeric,   -- sensitive
>   measurements jsonb,     -- sensitive: {"chest": ..., "waist": ..., etc.}
>   created_at   timestamptz default now()
> );
> alter table public.members enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own profile"
>   on public.members for select using (auth.uid() = id);
> create policy "member updates own profile"
>   on public.members for update using (auth.uid() = id);
> create policy "member inserts own profile"
>   on public.members for insert with check (auth.uid() = id);
>
> ---------- WORKOUTS ----------
> create table public.workouts (
>   id             uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
>   member_id      uuid not null references public.members(id) on delete cascade,
>   scheduled_date date not null,
>   title          text not null,
>   exercises      jsonb not null default '[]',
>   -- exercises shape: [{ name, sets_prescribed, reps_prescribed, notes }]
>   created_at     timestamptz default now()
> );
> alter table public.workouts enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own workouts"
>   on public.workouts for select using (auth.uid() = member_id);
> -- Coach creates workouts via an Edge Function using the service-role key.
> -- No client insert policy is needed.
>
> ---------- SETS ----------
> create table public.sets (
>   id            uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
>   workout_id    uuid not null references public.workouts(id) on delete cascade,
>   member_id     uuid not null references public.members(id) on delete cascade,
>   exercise_name text not null,
>   set_number    int  not null,
>   reps_completed int,
>   weight_kg     numeric,
>   notes         text,
>   logged_at     timestamptz default now()
> );
> alter table public.sets enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own sets"
>   on public.sets for select using (auth.uid() = member_id);
> create policy "member inserts own sets"
>   on public.sets for insert with check (auth.uid() = member_id);
> create policy "member updates own sets"
>   on public.sets for update using (auth.uid() = member_id);
>
> ---------- VIDEOS ----------
> create table public.videos (
>   id               uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
>   member_id        uuid not null references public.members(id) on delete cascade,
>   workout_id       uuid references public.workouts(id) on delete set null,
>   storage_path     text not null,  -- path inside the private Supabase bucket
>   ai_feedback      text,           -- written by Edge Function after analysis
>   feedback_status  text not null default 'pending'
>     check (feedback_status in ('pending', 'processing', 'done', 'error')),
>   created_at       timestamptz default now()
> );
> alter table public.videos enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own videos"
>   on public.videos for select using (auth.uid() = member_id);
> create policy "member inserts own videos"
>   on public.videos for insert with check (auth.uid() = member_id);
> -- MUST-NEVER rule: no cross-member select policy exists. Members can never
> -- see another member's videos.
>
> ---------- SUBSCRIPTIONS ----------
> create table public.subscriptions (
>   id                    uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),
>   member_id             uuid not null references public.members(id) on delete cascade,
>   revenuecat_customer_id text,
>   status                text not null default 'inactive'
>     check (status in ('active', 'inactive', 'past_due', 'cancelled')),
>   product_id            text,   -- e.g. "formcoach_monthly_999"
>   expires_at            timestamptz,
>   updated_at            timestamptz default now()
> );
> alter table public.subscriptions enable row level security;
> create policy "member reads own subscription"
>   on public.subscriptions for select using (auth.uid() = member_id);
> -- All subscription writes are done by the webhook Edge Function using the
> -- service-role key. No client write policy.
> ```

> -- Members can upload to their own folder (path must start with their user ID)
> create policy "member uploads own video"
>   on storage.objects for insert
>   with check (
>     bucket_id = 'videos'
>     and auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
>   );
>
> -- Members can read only their own video files
> create policy "member reads own video"
>   on storage.objects for select
>   using (
>     bucket_id = 'videos'
>     and auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]
>   );
>
> -- Members can delete their own video files (needed for account deletion)
> create policy "member deletes own video"
>   on storage.objects for delete

### S2.6 — AI form-check Edge Function

- [ ] **S2.6 AI form-check Edge Function**

**Goal:** A server-side function analyses the video using OpenAI Vision and writes feedback back to the `videos` table, enforcing the 5-checks-per-day limit. (Edge Functions are small programs that run on Supabase's servers, not inside the app — this is where the OpenAI key lives.)

**Build prompt:**

> Install the Supabase CLI:
> ```
> npm install -g supabase
> supabase init
> supabase login
> supabase link --project-ref YOUR_PROJECT_REF
> ```
> Find `YOUR_PROJECT_REF` in Supabase > Settings > General.
>
> Create `supabase/functions/analyze-form/index.ts`:
>
> ```ts
> import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.177.0/http/server.ts';
> import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2';
>
> serve(async (req) => {
>   // ── 1. Authenticate caller ──────────────────────────────────────────
>   const jwt = req.headers.get('Authorization')?.replace('Bearer ', '');
>   if (!jwt) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
>
>   const adminClient = createClient(
>     Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
>     Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!,
>   );
>   const userClient = createClient(
>     Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
>     Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_ANON_KEY')!,
>     { global: { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${jwt}` } } },
>   );
>   const { data: { user } } = await userClient.auth.getUser();
>   if (!user) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
>
>   // ── 2. Parse request body ───────────────────────────────────────────
>   const { video_id } = await req.json();
>   if (!video_id) return new Response('video_id required', { status: 400 });
>
>   // ── 3. Daily rate limit: max 5 form checks per member per day ───────
>   const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0];
>   const { count } = await adminClient
>     .from('videos')
>     .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
>     .eq('member_id', user.id)
>     .gte('created_at', `${today}T00:00:00Z`)
>     .in('feedback_status', ['processing', 'done']);
>
>   if ((count ?? 0) >= 5) {
>     return new Response(
>       JSON.stringify({ error: 'Daily limit of 5 form checks reached. Try again tomorrow.' }),
>       { status: 429, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } },
>     );
>   }
>
>   // ── 4. Confirm this video belongs to the requesting user ────────────
>   const { data: video } = await adminClient
>     .from('videos')
>     .select('storage_path, member_id')
>     .eq('id', video_id)
>     .single();
>
>   if (!video || video.member_id !== user.id) {
>     return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
>   }
>
>   // ── 5. Mark as processing ───────────────────────────────────────────
>   await adminClient.from('videos')
>     .update({ feedback_status: 'processing' })
>     .eq('id', video_id);
>
>   // ── 6. Generate a 60-second signed URL (never a public URL) ─────────
>   const { data: signed } = await adminClient.storage
>     .from('videos')
>     .createSignedUrl(video.storage_path, 60);
>
>   if (!signed?.signedUrl) {
>     await adminClient.from('videos')
>       .update({ feedback_status: 'error' }).eq('id', video_id);
>     return new Response('Could not access video', { status: 500 });
>   }
>
>   // ── 7. Call OpenAI Vision ────────────────────────────────────────────
>   const oaiRes = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
>     method: 'POST',
>     headers: {
>       Authorization: `Bearer ${Deno.env.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')}`,
>       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
>     },
>     body: JSON.stringify({
>       model: 'gpt-4o',
>       messages: [
>         {
>           role: 'system',
>           content: 'You are a certified strength coach reviewing a short exercise video. Give 2–3 specific, actionable coaching cues in plain English. Be encouraging but direct. Keep your total response under 120 words.',
>         },
>         {
>           role: 'user',
>           content: [
>             { type: 'text', text: 'Please review my exercise form.' },
>             { type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: signed.signedUrl } },
>           ],
>         },
>       ],
>       max_tokens: 200,
>     }),
>   });
>
>   const oaiJson  = await oaiRes.json();
>   const feedback = oaiJson.choices?.[0]?.message?.content ?? 'Unable to analyse video.';
>

### S3.3 — RevenueCat webhook + subscription verification

- [ ] **S3.3 Subscription verification (server-side webhook)**

**Goal:** Subscription status is updated in the database by a webhook from RevenueCat whenever a purchase, renewal, cancellation, or expiry event occurs. The app never trusts a status the app itself reports.

**Build prompt:**

> Create `supabase/functions/revenuecat-webhook/index.ts`:
>
> ```ts
> import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.177.0/http/server.ts';
> import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2';
>
> const WEBHOOK_SECRET = Deno.env.get('REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET')!;
> const adminClient   = createClient(
>   Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
>   Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!,
> );
>
> serve(async (req) => {
>   // Verify the shared secret RevenueCat sends in the Authorization header
>   if (req.headers.get('Authorization') !== `Bearer ${WEBHOOK_SECRET}`) {
>     return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
>   }
>
>   const body  = await req.json();
>   const event = body.event;
>   const { type, app_user_id, product_id, expiration_at_ms } = event;
>
>   const statusMap: Record<string, string> = {
>     INITIAL_PURCHASE: 'active',
>     RENEWAL:          'active',
>     UNCANCELLATION:   'active',
>     CANCELLATION:     'cancelled',
>     EXPIRATION:       'inactive',
>     BILLING_ISSUE:    'past_due',
>   };
>
>   const status = statusMap[type];
>   if (!status) return new Response('Event ignored', { status: 200 });
>
>   // app_user_id is the Supabase user UUID, set when we called Purchases.logIn(userId) in S3.1
>   await adminClient.from('subscriptions').upsert({
>     member_id:              app_user_id,
>     revenuecat_customer_id: event.original_app_user_id ?? app_user_id,
>     status,
>     product_id:             product_id ?? null,
>     expires_at:             expiration_at_ms ? new Date(expiration_at_ms).toISOString() : null,
>     updated_at:             new Date().toISOString(),
>   }, { onConflict: 'member_id' });
>
>   return new Response('OK', { status: 200 });
> });
> ```
>
> Set the webhook secret as a Supabase secret (never in app code):
> ```
> supabase secrets set REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET=choose-a-long-random-string
> ```
>
> Deploy:
> ```
> supabase functions deploy revenuecat-webhook --project-ref YOUR_PROJECT_REF
> ```
>
> In the RevenueCat dashboard > Project > Integrations > Webhooks:
> - URL: `https://YOUR_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co/functions/v1/revenuecat-webhook`
> - Authorization header value: the same string you set as `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

**How to test:**
1. In the RevenueCat dashboard, use "Send test event" and choose event type `INITIAL_PURCHASE`. Set `app_user_id` to your Supabase user UUID.
2. In Supabase > `subscriptions` table, confirm a row appears with `status = 'active'`.
3. Send a test `EXPIRATION` event — the row should update to `status = 'inactive'`.
4. Call the function URL directly without the Authorization header — confirm you get a 401 response.

**Done when:**
- Webhook upserts rows in `subscriptions` correctly for all six event types listed in `statusMap`.
- Wrong or missing secret returns 401.
- `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is in Supabase secrets only.

>   if (videos?.length) {
>     await adminClient.storage.from('videos').remove(videos.map(v => v.storage_path));
>   }
>
>   // Delete the auth user — ON DELETE CASCADE removes all rows in members,

>   const { error } = await adminClient.auth.admin.deleteUser(user.id);
>   if (error) return new Response('Deletion failed', { status: 500 });

> });
> ```

### S6.1 — Security audit

- [ ] **S6.1 Security audit — six checks**

**Goal:** Confirm every trust boundary from the architecture is enforced. Document the results.

**Build prompt:**

> Run each check below. Create `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` at the project root and record a ✅ PASS or ❌ FAIL + notes for each. Fix every FAIL before marking this slice done.
>
> ---
>
> **Check 1 — No secret keys in app code**
> Search every file under `src/`, `App.tsx`, `app.json`, and `eas.json` for these strings:
> - `sk-` (OpenAI key prefix)
> - `service_role`
> - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE`
> - `OPENAI_API_KEY`
> - `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
>
> None must appear. Only these four are allowed in app code:
> - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`
> - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
> - `EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY`
> - `EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY`
>
> ---
>
> **Check 2 — RLS enabled on every table**
> Run in Supabase SQL editor:
> ```sql
> select tablename, rowsecurity
> from pg_tables
> where schemaname = 'public'
> order by tablename;
> ```
> Every table must show `rowsecurity = true`. If any show `false`, run `alter table public.<tablename> enable row level security;`.
>
> ---
>
> **Check 3 — Cross-member data isolation**
> Create two test accounts: User A and User B. Log some sets for User A.
> While signed in as User B, open the Supabase JS client in a React Native debug console (or test via `curl` with User B's JWT) and run:
> ```ts
> const result = await supabase.from('sets').select('*').eq('member_id', USER_A_UUID);
> console.log(result.data); // must be [] or null — never User A's rows
> ```
> Repeat for `members`, `workouts`, `videos`, `subscriptions`.
> Also attempt to access User A's video file directly via storage using User B's session — must fail with an error.
>
> ---
>
> **Check 4 — Edge Function auth enforcement**
> Call each of the two Edge Functions without an `Authorization` header:
> ```bash
> curl -X POST https://YOUR_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co/functions/v1/analyze-form \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{"video_id":"fake"}'
> # Expected: 401 Unauthorized
>
> curl -X POST https://YOUR_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co/functions/v1/delete-account
> # Expected: 401 Unauthorized
> ```
>
> ---
>
> **Check 5 — Session token storage**
> Confirm in `src/lib/supabase.ts` that `storage: AsyncStorage` is set. On iOS, `AsyncStorage` data is stored in a SQLite database protected by iOS Data Protection (encrypted when the device is locked). Document this in `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`. Note: if a higher security requirement arises later, `expo-secure-store` can be used instead, but `AsyncStorage` with iOS Data Protection is sufficient for V1.
>
> ---
>
> **Check 6 — Video signed URLs are short-lived**
> In `supabase/functions/analyze-form/index.ts`, confirm the `createSignedUrl` call sets an expiry of 60 seconds:
> ```ts
> .createSignedUrl(video.storage_path, 60)  // ← must be 60, not 3600 or higher
> ```
> Confirm there are no `getPublicUrl` calls for the `videos` bucket anywhere in the codebase.

**How to test:**
1. `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` exists at the project root with a result for each of the 6 checks.
2. All 6 show ✅ PASS.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.

**Done when:**
- All 6 checks pass.
- `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` is committed.

## Findings Table

*(Technical terms explained on first use in the Plain-English risk column.)*

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 1 | Supabase **service role key** hardcoded in app bundle | **Critical** | `app.config.js` → `supabaseKey: 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.service_role.example'`; `src/lib/supabase.js` uses it for every query | The service role key is a master password for your database that **completely bypasses every RLS policy (Row Level Security — the per-table rules that restrict which rows each user can read or write)**. It is compiled into the app binary. Anyone who downloads the app, runs `npx expo export`, and inspects the JS bundle gets this key and can read, overwrite, or delete every user's plants, care logs, home addresses, and premium status without logging in. | Remove from `app.config.js`. Switch to the **anon key** (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) for the client. Keep the service role key only in Supabase Edge Function server environment variables (`Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')`), where it already lives correctly in `reset-password` and `admin-delete-user`. |
| 2 | OpenAI API key exposed in app bundle | **Critical** | `.env` line `EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY=sk-proj-example0000000000`; `src/lib/ai.js` `Authorization: Bearer ${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY}` | Any variable starting with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` is intentionally baked into the app binary by the Expo build system so the app can read it — but so can anyone else who unpacks the binary. The attacker extracts the key and calls OpenAI directly, charged to your account. With `gpt-4o` vision calls costing ~$0.01 each, a script running overnight can generate a four-figure bill. | Create a Supabase Edge Function called `diagnose`; move the `fetch('https://api.openai.com/…')` call there; read the key from `Deno.env.get('OPENAI_KEY')` (server-only). The app calls your Edge Function, never OpenAI directly. Delete `EXPO_PUBLIC_OPENAI_KEY` from `.env`. |
| 3 | Password-reset Edge Function has no authentication | **Critical** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts` — entire function body, zero token or identity check | The function accepts any `{ uid, newPassword }` JSON body and immediately resets that account's password. No session, no one-time token, no email proof. Any attacker who knows (or enumerates) a UUID — which Supabase exposes in several API responses — can POST `{"uid":"<victim>","newPassword":"hacked"}` and own that account in one request. This is a complete account-takeover endpoint. | Delete this function entirely. Use Supabase's built-in PKCE password-reset flow (PKCE = Proof Key for Code Exchange, a secure one-time handshake). The email link delivers a short-lived `code` parameter. In the app: `supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code)`, then `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: newPassword })`. Supabase validates the code server-side; no custom function needed. |
| 4 | Admin role stored in `user_metadata`, which users can edit themselves | **Critical** | `src/screens/Admin.js` line `user?.user_metadata?.role === 'admin'`; `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts` line `user?.user_metadata?.role !== 'admin'` | In Supabase, `user_metadata` is writable by the owner: any user can call `supabase.auth.updateUser({ data: { role: 'admin' } })`. After doing that, their JWT (JSON Web Token — the cryptographic login ticket the app sends with every request) will contain `role: admin`, and both the client-side `isAdmin()` check **and the server-side guard in `admin-delete-user`** will grant them admin power, including deleting any account. | Store roles in `app_metadata` — Supabase's field that **only the service role key can write**. Set it via the Supabase dashboard or a one-time server migration script. Replace every `user_metadata?.role` check with `app_metadata?.role`. The fix in `admin-delete-user` is one word change; the security improvement is total. |
| 5 | In-app purchase never verified server-side | **Critical** | `src/screens/Paywall.js` lines `if (purchase) {` → `supabase.from('profiles').update({ is_premium: true })` | The app decides premium is unlocked based on the local `purchase` object returned by the IAP library (IAP = In-App Purchase, the system for selling subscriptions inside mobile apps). That object is entirely client-side. Anyone can call the Supabase update directly — or patch the app — and set `is_premium = true` without a real payment. Even without reverse-engineering, issue #1 (service role key) already lets anyone do this today. | Create an Edge Function `verify-purchase`. Send the purchase `transactionReceipt` to it. The function calls Apple's `https://buy.itunes.apple.com/verifyReceipt` or Google's subscription validation API; **only if the receipt is valid** does it `UPDATE profiles SET is_premium = true`. Never set `is_premium` from the client at all — remove that column from the RLS update policy entirely (see issue #8). |

### 🚫 DO NOT SHIP

There are **7 Critical issues**, any one of which allows an attacker to cause immediate, serious harm:

- **Issue #1** (service role key in the app) means every user's data is readable and writable by anyone who downloads the app, right now, before any attacker needs to do anything clever.
- **Issue #3 + #11** together are a one-click account takeover of any user via a link.
- **Issue #4** lets any user make themselves an admin.
- **Issue #5** gives every user permanent premium access for free.
- **Issue #6** stores users' actual passwords in plain text on their phones.
- **Issue #7** exposes every user's home address and care history to every other logged-in user.

**2. DATABASE ACCESS — ISSUE** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`
`care_logs` has no `enable row level security` statement — RLS (database rules that automatically block access to rows a user doesn't own) is simply off for that table. **3. AUTHORIZATION — ISSUE** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`, `src/screens/Paywall.js`
The password-reset Edge Function (a small server-side function running in Supabase's cloud) accepts any `uid` and applies the new password with zero proof the caller owns that account. `buyPremium` writes `is_premium = true` to the database directly from the app with no server-side purchase verification.

**4. INPUT — ISSUE** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`
`newPassword` is passed straight to the admin SDK with no length or content check. No file type or size limits are visible for photo uploads.

**5. PAYMENTS — ISSUE** | `src/screens/Paywall.js`
After purchase, the app never sends the receipt to a server for Apple/Google verification. The client calls the database directly to flip the premium flag.

**6. AI/LLM — ISSUE** | `.env`, `src/lib/ai.js`
The OpenAI key is in the app bundle (item 1). Calls go device-to-OpenAI with no server in between, no per-user rate limit, and no server-side check that the caller is actually a premium user.

**7. RATE LIMITS & ABUSE — ISSUE** | no file
No rate limiting is visible on login, sign-up, password reset, or the AI diagnose endpoint.

**8. HEADERS & CORS — ISSUE** | `supabase/functions/reset-password/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`
Neither Edge Function sets CORS headers (rules that control which origins may call the endpoint) or any security response headers.

**9. DATA EXPOSURE — ISSUE** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`
`care_logs` has no RLS, so every authenticated user can query every other user's notes and home addresses. The service-role key in the bundle means all tables are fully open regardless of any RLS policies.

**10. DESTRUCTIVE OPS — ISSUE** | `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`, `src/screens/Admin.js`
The admin check reads `user_metadata` — a field any user can edit — before permitting account deletion.

**11. FILE STORAGE — ISSUE** | `supabase/storage.sql`
The `plant-photos` bucket is created with `public: true`, meaning every stored photo is accessible to any unauthenticated HTTP request that knows the path.

**12. ROLES — ISSUE** | `src/screens/Admin.js`, `supabase/functions/admin-delete-user/index.ts`
The admin flag lives in `user_metadata` — Supabase's user-editable metadata field. Any logged-in user can overwrite it via a standard Supabase API call. It should live in `app_metadata`, which only server-side admin code can write.

## Ship Verdict

**🚫 DO NOT SHIP**

There are **six Critical** vulnerabilities. The service role key alone (finding #1) renders every other database security control meaningless right now. Findings #3 and #5 together allow any user on the internet to take over any account and delete it with admin authority. Finding #6 means premium can be obtained for free by anyone. None of these require sophisticated exploitation — they are straightforward API calls.

**Fix all six Critical findings before any further testing. Then address the High findings before any public release.**

## 14-Item Security Check

**1. SECRETS** — OK (`/.env`, `src/supabase.js`)
`VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` is in the browser bundle by design — it is meant to be public, and every table it can reach is protected by Row Level Security (RLS — database-enforced rules that control which rows each user may read or change). The three real secrets (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) exist only in Supabase's server-side secrets store and never appear in client code.

**2. DATABASE ACCESS** — ISSUE (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`)
RLS is enabled on every table, and per-table policies match the intended access rules for all columns *except one*: `messages.sender_name` has no database-level constraint that ties it to the authenticated user's actual identity. The `"send as yourself"` policy only checks `from_id = auth.uid()`; it places no restriction on what string a user writes into `sender_name`.

**3. AUTHORIZATION** — ISSUE (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`, `src/pages/Messages.jsx`)
Checkout verifies the user JWT and fetches prices server-side ✓. The webhook verifies the Stripe signature before writing anything ✓. Storage is scoped to per-user folders ✓. However, message insertion permits any string as `sender_name`, so a logged-in user can impersonate "Admin", "Support Team", or any staff name in a message sent to another user.

**4. INPUT** — ISSUE (`src/pages/Files.jsx`)
React escapes all rendered text by default, so there is no XSS (Cross-Site Scripting — malicious code injected into a web page) risk from message content ✓. The 2,000-character cap on `messages.body` is enforced at the database level ✓. The file-type allow-list and 5 MB size limit in `Files.jsx` run *only* in the browser; a direct API call to Supabase Storage bypasses them entirely.

**5. PAYMENTS** — OK (`supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts`)
Prices are always fetched from the `services` table on the server; no price value travels from the browser. Stripe webhook signatures are verified with `constructEventAsync` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` before any booking record is touched. Booking status is written exclusively via the service-role key inside the webhook handler.

**6. AI/LLM** — NOT APPLICABLE
No AI or large-language-model features present in the codebase.

**7. RATE LIMITS & ABUSE** — ISSUE (`supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`)
No per-user rate limiting (a cap on how many times one user can call an endpoint within a time window) is applied to the checkout Edge Function. A logged-in user can loop-call it and open hundreds of Stripe checkout sessions in seconds, burning Stripe API quota and server compute. Supabase's built-in auth service handles login/signup rate limiting.

**8. HEADERS & CORS** — ISSUE (`supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`, hosting layer)
The checkout Edge Function sets no explicit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, so Supabase's platform default (which may allow any origin) applies. No Content-Security-Policy (CSP — a header that tells the browser which scripts and resources are trusted), `X-Frame-Options`, or other front-end security headers are shown anywhere in the codebase.

**9. DATA EXPOSURE** — OK
The checkout function returns only `{ url }`. RLS policies prevent one client from reading another's bookings or messages. The `stripe_session` value is visible to its booking owner but carries no standalone monetary risk.

**10. DESTRUCTIVE OPS** — OK (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`)
No DELETE policy exists on any table for client-facing roles. The `user_roles` table has no INSERT or UPDATE policy — clients cannot grant themselves elevated privileges. Destructive or administrative operations require the service-role key.

**11. FILE STORAGE** — OK (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`)
`client-files` is created with `public: false`. All file reads go through 60-second signed URLs (time-limited download links that expire automatically). Storage RLS policies enforce per-user folder isolation on both read and write.

**12. ROLES** — OK (`supabase/migrations/001_init.sql`)
Roles live in a server-side `user_roles` table with no client-writable policies. They are not stored in Supabase `user_metadata` (which the user can edit directly) or in browser storage.

**13. SENSITIVE DATA** — ISSUE (advisory) (`001_init.sql`, Storage bucket)
Booking records and Stripe session IDs are financial data. Uploaded files could include identity documents, invoices, or photos of people — the code places no label or audit trail on what is stored. No data-retention schedule or privacy notice is present.

**14. PHONE APP** — NOT APPLICABLE
Web-only application.

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 2 / 3 | `sender_name` not tied to the authenticated user's identity | **High** | `001_init.sql` — the `"send as yourself"` insert policy; `Messages.jsx` — the line rendering `{m.sender_name}` | Any logged-in user can insert `sender_name = 'Support Team'` (or any other name). The recipient sees bold "Support Team:" in the message thread, creating a convincing in-app phishing channel — for example, fake "click here to verify your account" messages. | **Option A (simplest):** drop the `sender_name` column; when reading messages join to a `profiles` table on `from_id` to get the real display name — the client never supplies it. **Option B:** keep the column but add a Postgres trigger that overwrites any client-supplied value: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lock_sender_name() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN NEW.sender_name := (SELECT email FROM auth.users WHERE id = NEW.from_id); RETURN NEW; END; $$; CREATE TRIGGER enforce_sender_name BEFORE INSERT ON messages FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION lock_sender_name();` |
| 4 | File type and size checks are browser-only | **Medium** | `src/pages/Files.jsx` lines `if (!ALLOWED.includes(file.type) \|\| file.size > 5_000_000)` | A user making a direct API call with curl or Postman skips these checks and can upload any file type or any size to their private folder. Because the bucket is private, per-user, and served only via short-lived signed URLs, the blast radius is limited to the attacker's own storage; the concrete risks are storage-cost abuse and upload of potentially malicious file types. | Set a hard upload-size cap in Supabase Dashboard → Storage → (bucket settings). For MIME enforcement, route all uploads through a short Edge Function that is the sole upload endpoint: receive the file, check `Content-Type` and byte-length server-side, then call the Storage API. |
| 7 | No rate limiting on the checkout endpoint | **Medium** | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — the entire request handler | A logged-in user can call this function in a tight loop, creating an unbounded number of Stripe checkout sessions and exhausting Stripe API quota and server CPU. | At the top of the handler, look up a `checkout_attempts` row for the user in a Supabase table (or Upstash Redis); if more than ~10 calls have occurred in the past 60 seconds, return `new Response('Too many requests', { status: 429 })` immediately. |
| 8 | No explicit CORS restriction; no front-end security headers | **Low** | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`; hosting / CDN config (not provided) | Without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://cleanbook.app`, any website can attempt to invoke the checkout function from a visitor's browser (though the attempt still requires the user's JWT, limiting practical risk). Without CSP and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, the front-end lacks declarative protection against script injection or clickjacking (loading the app in a hidden iframe to hijack clicks). | In the checkout function return: `headers: { 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': 'https://cleanbook.app', 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'authorization, content-type' }` and handle `OPTIONS` preflight. Set `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` via Vercel `vercel.json`, Netlify `_headers`, or your CDN's rules. The stripe-webhook function does not need CORS headers (it is called by Stripe's servers, not a browser). |
| 13 | Financial records and opaque file uploads with no retention policy or privacy notice | **Low** | `001_init.sql` — `bookings` table; Storage `client-files` bucket | Stripe session IDs and payment status are financial records. Uploaded files may contain ID documents, invoices, or photos — the code has no way to audit what is stored. Operating without a documented retention schedule and privacy notice is a compliance gap under GDPR, CCPA, and similar laws. | Document exactly what file types clients upload and why. Add a maximum retention period (e.g., delete files after 12 months via a scheduled Edge Function). Display a privacy notice at upload time. Commission a brief legal/privacy review before accepting EU or California users. |

---

## Ship Verdict

**FIX CRITICALS FIRST**

The single High issue — sender-name spoofing — takes less than an hour to resolve (drop the column or add the trigger) and must be done before launch, because it hands any logged-in user a ready-made tool to impersonate staff inside the app. The two Medium issues (browser-only file validation, no checkout rate limit) should land in the first post-launch sprint. The Low items are defence-in-depth hardening steps with no direct exploit path in the current code.

## 14-Item Security Check

*First use of a technical term is explained in plain English when it appears below.*

1. **SECRETS — ✓ OK** — `.env` exposes only `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, which is the Supabase *public key* — intentionally visible to every visitor, with database-level access rules doing the real guarding. `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` exist only in Supabase's server-side function secrets, never in the browser bundle.

2. **DATABASE ACCESS — ✓ OK** — Every table (`user_roles`, `services`, `bookings`, `messages`) and the storage-objects table has *Row Level Security* (RLS — a database setting that automatically enforces "can this logged-in user touch this row?") enabled. The only table with anonymous read access is `services`, which is the intentional public price list. All write paths go through the server.

3. **AUTHORIZATION — ✓ OK** — `checkout/index.ts` calls `sb.auth.getUser()` and returns 401 (access denied) if no valid user is found; the Stripe webhook skips user auth entirely and uses Stripe's *signature* (a cryptographic proof the request really came from Stripe) instead, which is the correct pattern; the messages insert policy enforces `from_id = auth.uid()` (the database row's "who sent this" column must match the logged-in user).

4. **INPUT — ⚠ ISSUE** — `Files.jsx` lines 3–4 validate file type and size in the browser only. The DB enforces message body length (≤ 2 000 characters). React escapes text content by default so there is no *XSS* (Cross-Site Scripting — injecting malicious code into a page other users see) risk in the messages component. *(See findings table.)*

5. **PAYMENTS — ✓ OK** — `stripe-webhook/index.ts` calls `stripe.webhooks.constructEventAsync` and returns 400 on a bad signature before touching any data. The price is fetched from the database inside the server function — the browser only sends a `serviceId`. Booking status is written exclusively by the webhook using the service-role key.

6. **AI / LLM — NOT APPLICABLE** — No AI or LLM features in the codebase.

7. **RATE LIMITS & ABUSE — ⚠ ISSUE** — No per-user rate limiting on the `checkout` Edge Function. The webhook is implicitly protected by Stripe's signature. *(See findings table.)*

8. **HEADERS & CORS — ⚠ ISSUE** — Neither Edge Function sets explicit *CORS headers* (browser rules that say which websites are allowed to talk to an endpoint) or handles the browser's *OPTIONS preflight* (a quick "are you allowed to do this?" check the browser fires before the real request). No frontend security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) are visible in the provided files. *(See findings table.)*

9. **DATA EXPOSURE — ⚠ ISSUE** — `sender_name` in the `messages` table is free text set by the client. The insert policy checks only that `from_id` matches the logged-in user; it does not verify that `sender_name` reflects the user's real identity. *(See findings table.)*

10. **DESTRUCTIVE OPS — ✓ OK** — No delete or admin-escalation endpoints are present in the provided code. Role writes have no client-facing policy.

11. **FILE STORAGE — ⚠ ISSUE** — The `client-files` bucket is private, per-user scoped, and files are served via 60-second *signed URLs* (time-limited, single-use download links that expire automatically) — all correct. However, the MIME-type and size limits live only in the browser (`Files.jsx` lines 3–4), not in the bucket's server configuration. *(Same root cause as item 4; one fix covers both — see findings table.)*

12. **ROLES — ✓ OK** — `user_roles` has no client `INSERT` or `UPDATE` policy; a logged-in user can only read their own role, never change it. Roles are not stored in user-editable metadata (e.g., Supabase `user_metadata` is writable by the user and is not used here).

13. **SENSITIVE DATA — ✓ OK** — Payment and booking records (financial data) are properly scoped by RLS. No children's, health, or education data is visible in the schema. A professional privacy/legal review is recommended before launch to confirm data-retention periods and whether financial records trigger any regional regulatory obligations.

14. **PHONE APP — NOT APPLICABLE** — Web-only application (Vite + React).

---

## Findings Table

*Plain-English severity guide: **Critical/High** = an attacker gets real data, money, or admin power right now. **Medium** = a real weakness, but existing controls limit the blast radius. **Low** = missing hardening that doesn't expose anything on its own.*

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 4 / 11 | File type and size validation is browser-only | **Medium** | `Files.jsx` lines 3–4 | A user can bypass the browser check (e.g., with `curl` or browser DevTools) and upload an HTML, SVG, or very large file to their folder. An admin who later opens that file via the signed URL could have scripts execute in their browser (on Supabase's storage domain). The private bucket and per-user scoping already limit who can reach the file; this fix removes the server-side blind spot. | In the Supabase Dashboard → Storage → `client-files` bucket → Edit: set **Allowed MIME types** to `application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg` and **File size limit** to `5000000` (5 MB). This is enforced by Supabase's storage server regardless of what the browser sends, making `Files.jsx`'s check a helpful UX layer rather than the only gate. |
| 9 | `sender_name` is not tied to the authenticated user's real identity | **Medium** | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — messages `INSERT` policy | Any logged-in user can send a message with `sender_name = 'Admin'` or `'Support Team'`. A client who receives that message sees what appears to be an official staff message, opening the door to in-platform phishing (e.g., "click here to verify your payment details"). | Remove `sender_name` from the columns the client controls on insert. Add a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `messages` that sets `sender_name = (SELECT display_name FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid())`, so the displayed name always reflects the verified account. Alternatively, derive it in a thin Edge Function wrapper that looks up the name server-side before inserting. |
| 7 | No rate limiting on the `checkout` Edge Function | **Low** | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` | A logged-in user could loop the endpoint, creating thousands of abandoned Stripe checkout sessions and potentially hitting Stripe's API rate limits or your Stripe plan's session quota. | Inside the function, read or increment a counter in a `rate_limit` table keyed on `(user_id, TRUNC(NOW(), 'minute'))` and return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) if the count exceeds ~10 per minute. Alternatively, use Supabase's built-in rate-limiting rules for the `/functions/v1/checkout` path. |
| 8 | CORS headers absent from the checkout Edge Function; security headers not visible for the frontend | **Low** | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`; frontend hosting config (not provided) | If CORS is later added carelessly as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, any website could make checkout requests using a logged-in user's token. Missing `X-Frame-Options` on the frontend leaves it open to *clickjacking* (embedding the site in an invisible frame to trick users into clicking things). | For the Edge Function, respond to `OPTIONS` requests with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://cleanbook.app` (your exact domain, not `*`) and the necessary `Allow-Headers`. For the frontend, set `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy` (a browser rule that restricts what scripts and resources a page can load), and `Strict-Transport-Security` (forces HTTPS) at your CDN or hosting provider. |

---

## Ship Verdict

**SHIP** — No Critical or High issues were found. ## 14-Item Security Check

**Term glossary (first use):** *RLS (Row Level Security)* = database rules that automatically filter which rows a user can read or write; *service role* = a special Supabase key that bypasses RLS, used only on the server; *signed URL* = a time-limited link that proves the storage service authorised this download; *JWT* = the login token issued by Supabase that every request carries to prove who the user is; *CORS* = the browser rule that decides which websites are allowed to call your API; *edge function* = serverless code that runs inside Supabase's infrastructure, not in the user's browser.

| # | Item | Result | File checked |
|---|------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | SECRETS | OK | `.env`, `checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts` — `VITE_` vars hold only the anon key (Supabase designs this to be public); Stripe and service-role keys live in Supabase function secrets, never in `.env` or any frontend file |
| 2 | DATABASE ACCESS | OK | `001_init.sql` — all four tables and the storage bucket have RLS enabled; every policy matches the stated access rules; no anonymous write path exists |
| 3 | AUTHORIZATION | OK | `checkout/index.ts` — JWT is verified with `auth.getUser()` (server-validates the signature, not just parses it) before any action; storage and message writes are gated by RLS on the server |
| 4 | INPUT | ISSUE | `Files.jsx` lines 4–5, `001_init.sql` messages table — file type/size check is browser-only; `sender_name` in messages has no server-side enforcement |
| 5 | PAYMENTS | OK | `checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts` — price is looked up from the database server-side; webhook signature is verified with `constructEventAsync` before the booking is written |
| 6 | AI/LLM | NOT APPLICABLE | No AI or LLM features present |
| 7 | RATE LIMITS & ABUSE | ISSUE | `checkout/index.ts` — no per-user rate limit on the Stripe session-creation endpoint |
| 8 | HEADERS & CORS | ISSUE | `checkout/index.ts`, `stripe-webhook/index.ts` — neither function sets explicit CORS restrictions or security headers |
| 9 | DATA EXPOSURE | OK | `checkout/index.ts` returns only `{url}`; every table query is scoped by RLS so responses contain only the calling user's own rows |
| 10 | DESTRUCTIVE OPS | NOT APPLICABLE | No delete or escalation paths are present in the provided code |
| 11 | FILE STORAGE | OK | `001_init.sql` — `client-files` bucket is `public: false`; every read goes through a 60-second signed URL; storage policies enforce per-user folder ownership |
| 12 | ROLES | OK | `001_init.sql` — roles live in a database table; no INSERT/UPDATE RLS policy means only the service role (server) can assign or change them; they are not in `user_metadata` or browser storage |
| 13 | SENSITIVE DATA | ISSUE | `001_init.sql` — financial records (Stripe session IDs, payment status) and uploaded client files are present; a professional privacy/legal review is recommended |
| 14 | PHONE APP | NOT APPLICABLE | Web-only app |

## Findings

| # | Issue | Severity | Where | Plain-English risk | Exact fix |
|---|-------|----------|-------|--------------------|-----------|
| 4a | `sender_name` is a free-text field the client sets at insert time; the RLS insert policy only enforces `from_id = auth.uid()` | Medium | `001_init.sql` — `create policy "send as yourself"` line; `Messages.jsx` renders it | A logged-in client can set `sender_name = "Admin"` or another person's real name, then send a message that appears to come from staff. This enables social engineering inside the platform. | Remove `sender_name` from the `messages` table and retrieve the display name at query time via a `JOIN` to a `profiles` table that users cannot write to directly. If you need a snapshot, write a Postgres trigger that overwrites `sender_name` with the authenticated user's canonical profile name on every INSERT. |
| 4b | File type and size are checked only in the browser (`Files.jsx` lines 4–5); a user calling the Supabase Storage API directly can skip this | Medium | `Files.jsx` lines 4–5; `001_init.sql` storage policies do not restrict MIME type or size | A user can upload any file type (e.g. a `.exe` disguised as a PDF) into their private folder by calling the API directly. Staff or admins who later review client files via a service-role query could be tricked into opening a malicious file. Bucket-level cost controls are also bypassed. | In the Supabase dashboard set a 5 MB file-size limit on the `client-files` bucket. For MIME type, add a thin Edge Function that proxies uploads, reads the first bytes of the file to verify the actual content type, and rejects anything outside `application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg` before forwarding to storage. |
| 7 | The `checkout` Edge Function has no per-user call limit | Medium | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — the entire function body | An authenticated user can call the endpoint in a tight loop, generating hundreds of open Stripe Checkout sessions. This can exhaust your Stripe API rate quota and inflate billing even if no payment is made. | Track calls with a lightweight counter: store a `(user_id, minute_bucket, count)` row in a `rate_limits` table using the service-role client; if `count > 5` within a minute return HTTP 429. Alternatively, enable Supabase's built-in Edge Function rate limiting in the project dashboard (Auth → Rate limits). |
| 8 | Edge functions return no CORS restrictions or security response headers | Low | `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts`, `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` | Without an explicit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header the browser falls back to the runtime default, which in some Supabase versions is `*` (any site). A missing `X-Content-Type-Options` or `Content-Security-Policy` is defence-in-depth that is absent. | At the top of each `Deno.serve` handler return a preflight response and add headers: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://cleanbook.app`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000`. The stripe-webhook endpoint should additionally reject all `OPTIONS` preflight requests with 405, since it should never be called from a browser. |
| 13 | The app stores financial records (Stripe session IDs, payment status) and accepts arbitrary uploaded files that may include personal ID documents | Low | `001_init.sql` — `bookings` table; `client-files` storage bucket | Depending on your jurisdiction, storing payment records and personal documents triggers GDPR, CCPA, or PCI-DSS obligations around retention periods, right-to-erasure, and data-processing agreements. The current schema has no expiry or deletion path for either. | Engage a privacy/legal reviewer before going live with real customers. At minimum: document a data-retention policy; add a `deleted_at` soft-delete column to `bookings`; confirm your Supabase data-processing agreement is signed; make sure the Stripe integration is using Stripe's PCI-compliant hosted page (it is — `checkout.sessions.create` is correct). |

---

## Ship verdict

**SHIP** — The core security architecture is solid: prices are enforced server-side, the Stripe webhook is signature-verified, RLS protects every table, roles cannot be self-assigned, and personal files are served through short-lived signed URLs. None of the issues above let an attacker read someone else's data, fake a payment, or gain elevated access. Fix items 4a and 4b before you handle any real customer files, and address 7 before you expect meaningful traffic.
